title: PM to participate in Valedictory Session of Departmental Summit on Women and Child Development on 9th October
subtitle: Summit to Focus on Key Themes of Nutrition, Early Education, Child Protection, Women’s Safety and Empowerment
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                08 OCT 2026 4:44PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi will participate in the valedictory session of Departmental Summit on Women and Child Development on 9th October 2026 at around 4:30 PM at Sushma Swaraj Bhawan, New Delhi. He will also address the gathering on the occasion.
The two-day Departmental Summit, being held on 8-9 October 2026, will witness participation of political leadership and officials dealing with the women and child development sector from all States. It is the second in the series of Departmental Summits envisioned by the Prime Minister to strengthen cooperative federalism, foster collective ownership of national priorities, and accelerate outcomes through closer Centre-State collaboration.
The Summit will focus on four themes:
Reimagining Anganwadi Centres for better nutrition and early education
Strengthening the protection system for vulnerable children
Women’s safety through effective implementation of institutional and legislative frameworks
Women’s empowerment through enhancing the effectiveness and outcomes of key schemes.
The Departmental Summit model brings together stakeholders from the Union and State Governments to deliberate on sectoral priorities, share good practices, address implementation challenges, and agree on time-bound actions for improved governance and service delivery.

title: Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi inaugurates 10th edition of India Mobile Congress
subtitle:
It is encouraging to see India's telecom sector steadily moving towards greater self-reliance: PM


Over the past 10-12 years, the mobile phone, along with being a medium of modern communication, has also emerged as a crucial tool for good governance, and this has been at the core of our Digital India vision: PM

Up until a decade ago, the digital divide was a major challenge in India; Modern technology was increasingly becoming a privilege; only those with means could reap the benefits of modern technology, this was the scenario unfolding in India; With the Digital India campaign, we decided to change this reality, and placed the mobile phone at its center; This was a massive endeavor towards the democratization of technology: PM

Today, hundreds of government services can be accessed on mobile phones; Government aid is now transferred directly into the accounts of the beneficiaries: PM

Mobile phones are no longer just a medium to chat, rather, they have ensured less travel, less waiting, less cost, and more convenience;This is technology's biggest Citizen dividend: PM

In India, the mobile phone today, acts as both a gaming console, and a creation studio: PM

Given the critical importance of telecom and digital technology today, it is vital to fortify its security framework, Phone and network security, is a priority for all of us: PM

We are all witnessing the major challenge that Deepfakes have become, That is why it is crucial to work on a Global Framework to tackle this: PM

Over the past few years, India has traversed the journey from a Consumer to a Creator; Now, India is marching towards the goal, where the product and design will be made in India, and its technology and IP will also belong to India: PM
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                08 OCT 2026 2:07PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi inaugurated the 10th edition of the India Mobile Congress (IMC) today at Yashobhoomi, New Delhi. Commemorating a deeply significant national milestone, the Prime Minister honored October 8th as Air Force Day, dedicating his opening thoughts to the nation's brave aerial defenders. He proudly offered his salutations to the courageous personnel safeguarding the skies."I bow to all our bravehearts and wish the country on Air Force Day,” affirmed Shri Modi.
Reflecting on a monumental personal milestone, the Prime Minister shared his deep gratitude for completing exactly 25 years of continuous service as a Head of Government just the day prior. He warmly thanked every citizen and international friend who supported him throughout this natural journey of public service."I express my gratitude to every countryman and every friend of India around the world for their good wishes,” remarked Shri Modi.
Highlighting a wonderful parallel of longevity, the Prime Minister celebrated the 10th anniversary of the India Mobile Congress while simultaneously noting the distinct honor of hosting the GSMA Board meeting in the country. He extended a wholehearted welcome to the entire global ecosystem of telecom operators, industry leaders, academics, and startups present.
Addressing  with a heavy heart, the Prime Minister shared the somber morning news regarding the passing of the legendary actor Nana Patekar. He praised the brilliant artist for consistently winning the audience's hearts by bringing a diverse array of characters to life on screen. "He was a brilliant artist who won the hearts of audiences through different characters,” remarked Shri Modi.
Eulogizing the late actor's profound national spirit, the Prime Minister described Nana Patekar as a fiercely independent soul whose life was entirely dedicated to the honor and glory of the tricolor. He characterized the late actor as a cinematic revolutionary whose sharp dialogue and powerful silence relentlessly struck against societal evils and anti-national elements."I pay my tributes to Nana Patekar ji and express my condolences to his family members and admirers,” affirmed Shri Modi.
Tracing the remarkable evolution of digital connectivity through the lens of the India Mobile Congress, the Prime Minister recalled launching 5G from the very same stage in 2022 and predicting its massive expansion in 2023. He proudly announced that 5G networks, now operating from over 5.5 lakh base stations, have successfully reached every single district, boosting internet speeds tenfold. "Today we all are seeing 5G connectivity has reached every district of the country,” asserted Shri Modi.
Reflecting on the platform's rising global stature, the Prime Minister recalled how the 2024 edition hosted the International Telecommunication Union to discuss global standards, while previous years focused heavily on domestic innovation and manufacturing. He credited the India Mobile Congress for emerging as a crucial catalyst for the nation's soaring telecom success and realizing its grandest dreams."In the past years, this platform has emerged as the platform of India's progress, of India's dreams,” noted Shri Modi.
Embracing the summit's ambitious theme, the Prime Minister challenged the delegates to look at the nation's own transformative journey as the ultimate proof of scaling without boundaries. He promised to share how the country actively lived and executed this exact vision of limitless expansion."I would like to tell you from India's experiences how we have lived and demonstrated the dream of Scale without boundaries,” remarked Shri Modi.
Redefining the fundamental purpose of connectivity, the Prime Minister explained that while global telecom debates obsess over spectrum, towers, and network speeds, the mobile phone has evolved into something far more profound for the domestic population."In the last 10-12 years, the mobile phone has emerged as a vital tool of good governance, serving as the absolute core of the Digital India vision” asserted Shri Modi.'
Addressing the foundational motives behind the telecom boom, the Prime Minister acknowledged global amazement regarding the nation's data, affordable devices, and massive user base, but urged the audience to understand the deeper 'why' and 'how' behind these achievements. He explained that comprehending this underlying purpose reveals the exact focus area driving the nation forward. "When we understand this, everyone will find India's focus area crystal clear,” noted Shri Modi.
Detailing the aggressive battle against digital exclusion, the Prime Minister recalled how modern technology was rapidly becoming an elite privilege just a decade ago. He explained that the Digital India campaign deliberately centralized the mobile phone to fiercely democratize technology, executing sweeping telecom reforms and vastly expanding infrastructure to ensure devices were manufactured domestically. "This was a very big effort for the democratization of technology,” affirmed Shri Modi.
Showcasing the resilience forged by this digital democratization, the Prime Minister highlighted how widespread access to mobile phones and data drastically improved the Ease of Living for common citizens, famously keeping offices, banks, and schools running seamlessly during the global pandemic shutdowns. He celebrated how even the poorest children in remote villages can now effortlessly access quality digital education. "Digital learning is coming within everyone's reach,” asserted Shri Modi.
Presenting staggering metrics to validate this educational revolution, the Prime Minister shared data from the national Diksha online platform. He revealed that during the peak of the pandemic up to July 2022, the platform facilitated over 5 billion learning sessions and 60 billion learning minutes."Now our effort is to connect about 25 crore students with all our digital and online education mediums,” affirmed Shri Modi.
Explaining how technology unified a vastly heterogeneous nation, the Prime Minister noted that mobile connectivity systematically dismantled the immense geographic and linguistic barriers that previously hindered daily life. He highlighted that before the digital shift, citizens wasted massive amounts of time and money traveling to urban centers just to access basic banking, healthcare, and government services."Mobile connectivity has connected this diversity with convenience as well,” observed Shri Modi.
Detailing the monumental financial integrity achieved through digital governance, the Prime Minister proudly stated that over 50 lakh crore rupees have been transferred directly to beneficiaries via mobile platforms, effectively preventing 5 lakh crore rupees from leaking into corrupt hands. He specifically highlighted the PM Kisan Samman Nidhi, which has securely deposited over 4 lakh crore rupees directly to marginalized small farmers who previously never saw government benefits."Now that same money is reaching the right beneficiary,” asserted Shri Modi.
Summarizing the ultimate philosophy behind this technological empowerment, the Prime Minister declared that mobile phones transcended simple chatting to guarantee less travel, less waiting, lower costs, and vastly more convenience. He branded this sweeping holistic transformation as the ultimate return on technological investment for the common man." This is Technology's biggest Citizen Dividend,” affirmed Shri Modi.
Highlighting the economic chain reaction triggered by robust infrastructure, the Prime Minister explained how remote tower installations, massive optical fiber rollouts, and cheap data birthed entirely new sectors in the economy. He noted that this foundational expansion generated a massive wave of new consumers and creators across technology, entertainment, and education. "This has also created new sectors in the economy,” noted Shri Modi.
Spotlighting the explosive growth of the interactive entertainment sector, the Prime Minister shared that over 50 crore people, heavily concentrated among the youth in Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities, are now actively engaged in the gaming ecosystem. He praised these young digital natives for evolving from mere players into competitive e-sports athletes, content creators, and ambitious business owners."Meaning, the mobile phone in India is today a gaming console as well and has also become a studio of creation,” remarked Shri Modi.
Celebrating the democratization of the creator economy, the Prime Minister explained how rapid connectivity and affordable data successfully pushed video-sharing platforms and regional OTT services deep into rural towns, breaking down historical language barriers. He revealed that the content creation industry alone has ballooned into a multi-thousand-crore sector, providing lucrative livelihoods for millions."Meaning, the mobile phone has also democratized content creation in India,” asserted Shri Modi.
Pivoting to the critical imperative of cybersecurity, the Prime Minister stressed that as telecom and digital technologies become fundamental to daily life, fortifying the security framework surrounding phones and networks is an absolute national priority. He emphasized that for the common citizen, complex architectural protocols matter far less than the simple, fundamental assurance of safety."For him, trust is very important,” noted Shri Modi.
Detailing the granular expectations of digital trust, the Prime Minister painted a clear picture of user security, insisting that citizens must absolutely know the true identity of callers, verify the authenticity of messages, and feel entirely secure when executing payments or sharing personal data. He made it clear that consumer confidence is the absolute bedrock of digital expansion."When he provides his data in any form, he should have the trust that his data is safe,” affirmed Shri Modi.
Calling for unified international action against borderless digital threats, the Prime Minister warned that cyber fraud and deepfakes exploit global vulnerabilities, requiring an urgent, coordinated Global Framework uniting governments, tech companies, operators, and financial institutions. He explicitly challenged the GSMA to help engineer proactive mechanisms capable of intercepting fraud before it ever reaches the end user."India is always ready to share its experiences with the world,” asserted Shri Modi.
Focusing on the strategic horizon, the Prime Minister reminded the delegates that with only four years left in the current decade, their immediate summit discussions will forge the crucial roadmap guiding the global mobile market into the future. He framed the event as a pivotal planning ground for the next era of technological dominance." This roadmap will give direction to the mobile market of the entire world along with India,” noted Shri Modi.
Outlining the ultimate vision for technological sovereignty, the Prime Minister declared that the nation has successfully transitioned from a consumer to a creator, and is now aggressively charging toward complete domestic control over product design, underlying technology, and intellectual property. He assured the industry that the government is rapidly modernizing decades-old laws, deploying comprehensive incentives, and executing sweeping regulatory reforms like the Telecommunications Act and the GatiShakti portal to ensure success."Meaning, in the telecom sector as well, the reform express is moving forward rapidly,” asserted Shri Modi.
Providing an update on critical hardware localization, the Prime Minister announced that the domestic semiconductor manufacturing ecosystem is accelerating rapidly, with commercial production already live across five locations. He declared that the next phase of the India Semiconductor Mission will aggressively target the localization of the entire supply chain."Meaning, India is taking big steps in every area related to the telecom sector,” affirmed Shri Modi.
Concluding his address with a soaring call to action, the Prime Minister challenged the India Mobile Congress to transcend being a mere technology showcase and instead become the ultimate crucible for humanity-serving innovations, research, and partnerships that will power the grand resolution of a developed nation. He expressed his expectation that the attendees will tirelessly strive to transform the platform into the premier global junction for industry and ideas."I am confident that you all will keep making wholehearted efforts for this, with this expectation, once again, many best wishes to all of you,” remarked Shri Modi.

title: English rendering of PM’s address at the inauguration of 10th edition of the India Mobile Congress
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                08 OCT 2026 1:05PM by PIB Delhi
content:
My colleagues in the Union Cabinet, Jyotiraditya Scindia Ji, Minister of State Chandrasekhar Pemmasani Ji, ministers from various state governments, all members of the GSMA Board, representatives of telecom operators from across the world, industry leaders, experts, my young friends who have come from different colleges and startups across the country, ladies and gentlemen.
Today is October 8, a special day for India. We celebrate this day as Air Force Day. I pay my respects to all our brave Air Warriors and extend my greetings to the nation on Air Force Day.
Friends,
As Scindia Ji just mentioned, only yesterday I completed 25 years of serving the nation as the Head of Government. For me, this has been a natural and continuous journey of service. I express my gratitude to every citizen of the country and every friend of India across the world for their good wishes.
Friends,
It is also a coincidence that on this occasion, the India Mobile Congress is completing ten years. This year, India was chosen to host the GSMA Board meeting. I welcome and congratulate all of you representatives of telecom operators, industry leaders, experts, academia, and startups who have come here from across the world.
Friends,
This very morning, we received the news that the renowned actor Nana Patekar Ji is no longer among us. He was an outstanding artist who won the hearts of audiences through a wide range of roles. Nana Patekar Ji dedicated his life to the honour, pride, and glory of the Tricolour. He never allowed himself to be confined; like a bird, he soared across the skies of cinema. Through his films, he launched powerful attacks on disorder and injustice in society. He was a true revolutionary who worked against social evils. His words were powerful, and his silence was equally impactful. He consistently supported firm action against those who worked against the nation. I pay my tribute to Nana Patekar Ji and express my condolences to his family members and admirers.
Friends,
I have had the opportunity to join you at several editions of the India Mobile Congress. This platform has witnessed how the telecom sector and digital connectivity have evolved. In 2022, from this very stage, we launched 5G in the country. In 2023, I spoke about how India was moving from 5G Roll-out to 5G Reach-out. Today, we can all see that 5G connectivity has reached every district of the country. More than 550,000 base stations are now operating across India, providing 5G services. Mobile internet speeds have increased tenfold compared to 2022.
Friends,
At the 2024 edition of India Mobile Congress, we witnessed the presence of the International Telecommunication Union (ITU). At that time, we discussed the need for global standards for the digital world. Last year, we deliberated on Invest, Innovate, and Make in India. The position that India has achieved today in the telecom sector owes much to India Mobile Congress. Over the years, this platform has emerged as a stage for India's progress and India's aspirations. Therefore, I extend special congratulations to all of you.
Friends,
This year, you have chosen the theme of your deliberations as "Scale Without Boundaries." I would like to share India's experience of how we have turned the dream of scaling beyond boundaries into a reality.
Friends,
When we talk about telecom, discussions often revolve around networks, spectrum debates, towers, reach, and speed. But for the people of India, telecom has meant much more. Over the past decade, the mobile phone has emerged not only as a tool of modern communication but also as an important instrument of good governance. This has remained at the core of our Digital India vision.
Friends,
Today, we hear that data in India is affordable, mobile phones are affordable, and the user base has expanded dramatically. All of this is true. But how did it happen? And why was all this done? When we understand this, India's focus and priorities become crystal clear.
Friends,
Until a decade ago, the digital divide was a major challenge in India. Modern technology was increasingly becoming a privilege. In other words, only those with resources could benefit from modern technology. India was also moving in that direction. Through the Digital India campaign, we resolved to change this situation and placed the mobile phone at its centre. This was a major effort towards the democratization of technology. For this purpose, all necessary reforms were carried out in the telecom sector and infrastructure was expanded. We also focused on ensuring that mobile phones and other telecom hardware would be manufactured in India itself.
Friends,
As a result of these efforts, mobile phones and data became far more accessible and affordable for ordinary Indians. Today, this is enhancing the ease of living of our citizens. During the COVID period, we witnessed how almost everything came to a standstill. Yet offices continued functioning, banks remained operational, and education continued in India. This was made possible by India's digital ecosystem. Mobile and internet connectivity ensured uninterrupted access to education, healthcare, payments, and government services. Today, even children from remote villages and underprivileged backgrounds can access quality knowledge. Digital learning is increasingly becoming accessible to everyone.
Friends,
Let me share a statistic that further demonstrates the impact of Digital India. We have a platform called DIKSHA for online education. During the COVID period, by July 2022, more than 5 billion learning sessions and nearly 600 billion learning minutes had been recorded on this platform. Our effort now is to connect nearly 250 million students to all our digital and online education platforms.
In other words, friends,
The revolution in the telecom sector has directly benefited Indian citizens. As you know, India is diverse in every sense, in language as well as geography. Such diversity can also create many inconveniences in people's lives. Mobile connectivity has transformed this diversity into convenience. Earlier, most banks were located in cities, hospitals were concentrated in urban areas, and government offices were typically available only at block or district headquarters. Any government service required significant investment of both time and money. Digital governance has changed these conditions. Today, hundreds of government services are available through mobile phones. Government assistance is now transferred directly to beneficiaries' accounts. Through Direct Benefit Transfer, nearly ₹50 lakh crore has reached beneficiaries directly in their bank accounts. As a result, nearly ₹5 lakh crore has been prevented from falling into the wrong hands. This is not a small figure. Nearly ₹5 lakh crore has been saved from misuse.
Now tell me, those whose easy earnings have stopped, will they love Modi? Did I do the right thing or not? Should this have been done or not? Should such wrong practices be stopped or not? They may shout and scream as much as they want, but I have made up my mind and I will continue in this direction.
If the old system had remained in place, around ₹5 lakh crore of government money would have been lost through leakages and would have filled the pockets of such people. We stopped this. Now that money reaches the rightful beneficiary, and the savings are being utilized for productive purposes.
Friends,
Under the PM-Kisan Samman Nidhi scheme, we have already deposited more than ₹4 lakh crore directly into the bank accounts of farmers. This amount is transferred every four months, and the farmer receives a notification directly on his mobile phone. This money has reached crores of small farmers who, in the past, often remained beyond the reach of government schemes.
In other words, friends,
The mobile phone is no longer merely a medium for communication. It has ensured less travel, less waiting, less cost, and greater convenience. This is the greatest citizen dividend that technology can deliver.
Friends,
Over the past decade, India's telecom infrastructure has expanded continuously. Towers have been installed in remote areas, optical fibre networks have expanded on an unprecedented scale, and data has become more affordable. This has also given rise to entirely new sectors of the economy. It has created new consumers in technology, entertainment, and education, while simultaneously nurturing a new generation of creators. Take gaming as an example. It is estimated that today more than 500 million people in India are connected to the gaming ecosystem in one way or another. A large proportion of them are young Indians. Youth from Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities are also actively participating. They are not only playing games but competing in e-sports, creating gaming content, and building new gaming businesses. In other words, the mobile phone in India has become both a gaming console and a creation studio.
Friends,
The telecom revolution in India has brought a similar transformation in the world of content. Better and faster connectivity, coupled with affordable data, has taken video-sharing platforms, social media, and regional OTT services to villages and small towns. As a result, many language-related barriers and limitations have been removed. Today, the content creation industry alone is worth thousands of crores of rupees in India and provides income opportunities for millions of people. In other words, the mobile phone has democratized content creation in India.
Friends,
At a time when telecom and digital technology are playing such a critical role, it is equally important that we strengthen the security framework associated with them. The security of phones and the security of networks are priorities for all of us. An ordinary citizen does not think in terms of protocols or architecture; for them, trust is what matters most. When they receive a call, they should know who is calling. When they receive a message, they should know whether it is genuine or fake. When they make a payment, they should be confident that their money is secure. When they provide their data through a form, they should know that their information is protected.
Friends,
Technology achieves scale only when it earns trust. And we all know that cyber fraud and cybercrime do not respect borders. They have already crossed boundaries. A person sitting in one country may commit a crime in a third country with assistance from a second country. We are also witnessing how serious a challenge deepfakes have become. Therefore, it is necessary that we work on a global framework to address these issues. Governments, technology companies, telecom operators, and financial institutions must all become part of such a framework. I would also urge GSMA and telecom operators around the world to come together and create a global mechanism that can stop such fraud even before it reaches people. India has learned a great deal through its own experiences, and India is always ready to share those experiences with the world.
Friends,
Only four years remain in this decade. The discussions that take place at this edition of India Mobile Congress will strengthen the roadmap for the next decade. And this roadmap will guide not only India but the global mobile market as well. Over the past years, India has progressed from being a consumer to becoming a creator. Now India is moving towards a future where products and designs will originate in India, and their technology and intellectual property will also belong to India. To achieve this, every necessary incentive is being provided and every necessary reform is being undertaken. In other words, the reform express is moving rapidly forward in the telecom sector as well. We are modernizing laws that are decades old. Through the Telecommunications Act, we have created a modern regulatory framework. We are also rationalizing structural burdens such as AGR and bank guarantees, transforming burdens into opportunities. The GatiShakti Sanchar Portal has accelerated Right of Way approvals through digital processes.
Friends,
India's semiconductor and semiconductor manufacturing ecosystem is also gathering momentum. Commercial production has already started at five locations. In the next phase of the India Semiconductor Mission, our focus will be on the entire supply chain. In other words, India is taking major strides in every area associated with the telecom sector.
Friends,
Over the years, India Mobile Congress has achieved a great deal. However, the journey of development is one of continuously crossing new milestones. We have before us the grand resolve of a Developed India, and for that we must continuously broaden our efforts. The technologies showcased here certainly have their own importance. But IMC should be remembered for the partnerships that were forged here, for the research projects that were launched here, for the products that reached the world from here, and for the innovations that emerged from India and served humanity. We must transform IMC into a platform that serves as a junction for technology, research, industry, investment, and ideas. I am confident that all of you will continue to work towards this goal with complete dedication. With this expectation, I once again extend my heartfelt congratulations and best wishes to all of you.
Thank you very much.
DISCLAIMER: This is the approximate translation of Prime Minister’s address. Original address was delivered in Hindi.

title: Women Account for 43% of Overall Ayush Services Workforce; Representation Exceeds 50% Across Several Organised Segments
subtitle:
Female Representation Crosses 50% in Hospitals, Day-Care Centres, Educational Institutes and Wellness Establishments

Ayush Services Sector Supports 1.76 Million Livelihoods, Emerges as a Significant Engine of Employment and Economic Growth
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                08 OCT 2026 12:33PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Ayush services sector is emerging as an important avenue for women’s participation in the workforce, with female representation exceeding 50 per cent across several organised segments, according to a recent assessment of the sector. Women account for 43 per cent of the overall Ayush services workforce, with their representation crossing 50 per cent in hospitals, day-care centres, educational institutes and wellness establishments.
The Ayush services economy, covering Ayurveda, Yoga & Naturopathy, Unani, Siddha, Sowa-Rigpa and Homoeopathy, was estimated at US$36.92 billion in FY2024-25, registering a robust 16.91 per cent CAGR since FY2022-23. The sector directly supports an estimated
1.76 million livelihoods
across healthcare, wellness, education and allied services.
Highlighting the employment potential of the sector, Shri Prataprao Jadhav, Union Minister of State (IC) for Ayush and Minister of State for Health & Family Welfare, reiterated, “The growing Ayush services sector is creating meaningful employment opportunities across healthcare, wellness, education and allied services. Its expansion is not only strengthening India’s healthcare ecosystem but also opening new avenues for entrepreneurship, skill development and women’s participation in the workforce.”
According to the Ayush Service Sector Report, a study by RIS released recently on Ayurveda Day 2026, women’s participation is particularly significant across organised Ayush establishments. Female representation exceeds 60 per cent in spas and wellness resorts, stands at 58 per cent in educational institutes, 57 per cent in day-care centres and 53 per cent in hospitals.
The findings highlight the growing role of women across diverse segments of the Ayush services ecosystem, including healthcare delivery, education, wellness and allied services. More than one million livelihoods are concentrated in local and standalone clinics, demonstrating the sector’s extensive employment footprint across urban and rural areas.
Secretary, Ministry of Ayush Vaidya Rajesh Kotecha emphasised, “The expansion of organised Ayush services, supported by quality standards, skilling, digital infrastructure and stronger institutional networks, can significantly enhance both the scale and quality of employment. Greater participation of women in organised Ayush establishments also demonstrates the sector’s potential to contribute to inclusive economic growth.”
Standalone clinics remain the largest revenue-generating segment, contributing an estimated US$16.21 billion, or 43.9 per cent of the sector’s revenue, while day-care centres account for another US$10.13 billion. Together, the two segments contribute more than 70 per cent of the sector’s revenue. Ayurveda remains the largest individual system, accounting for US$17.73 billion, or around 48 per cent of the total Ayush services revenue.
The wellness segment is witnessing particularly strong growth, recording a 21.29 per cent CAGR; meanwhile, Yoga centres registered around 75 per cent revenue growth over two years, reflecting rising demand for preventive health and wellness services.
The sector is also gaining traction in Medical Value Travel (MVT), generating an estimated US$1.77 billion in FY2024-25. International patients, though accounting for around 5 per cent of patient volumes, contribute approximately 15-25 per cent of hospital segment revenue, with therapeutic programmes typically involving stays of 5 to 11 days.
The assessment projects the Ayush services sector to expand from US 36.92 billion in FY 2024–25 to an estimated US 216–318 billion by 2047, with substantial potential to generate employment opportunities across diverse areas, including healthcare delivery, wellness, education, medical travel, research, digital health and allied services.
The growing representation of women across organised Ayush establishments, alongside the sector’s expanding economic and employment footprint, highlights its potential to contribute to women’s economic participation, inclusive growth and India’s broader development journey towards Viksit Bharat@2047.

title: Opening of Space Sector to Private Players Has Helped Reduce Brain Drain, Created New Opportunities for Young Talent: Dr Jitendra Singh
subtitle:
India’s Space Ecosystem No Longer Limited to Government Sector; Startups and Private Players Are Creating Opportunities for Young Engineers Within the Country, Says Dr. Jitendra Singh

“The Age of Silos Is Over”: Government, Industry, Startups and Academia Must Work Together to Build India’s Scientific Strength: Dr. Jitendra Singh

Space Technology Is No Longer Limited to Rockets and Missions; It Is Making Everyday Life Easier Through Disaster Management and Infrastructure Planning, Says Dr. Jitendra Singh

India Has Moved from Following the World to Moving Alongside It in Science and Technology: Dr Jitendra Singh
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                08 OCT 2026 5:12PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The opening of India’s space sector to private players has created new opportunities for young scientific and technical talent within the country and helped reduce the need to look abroad for employment, Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science & Technology and Earth Sciences and MoS PMO, Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions, Atomic Energy and Space, Dr Jitendra Singh, said today.
Dr Jitendra Singh was addressing students at the NaMo Book Fest at the Rudraksh International Cooperation and Convention Centre, Varanasi, a two-day festival being held on October 7-8 and commemorating 25 years of Prime Minister Narendra Modi as Head of Government, through books written by different authors on various facets of his life, leadership and public service. The festival was coordinated by senior journalist Ashok Shrivastava.
Later, interacting with students in a question-answer session, Dr Jitendra Singh said that earlier, limited opportunities within the domestic space ecosystem meant that many young professionals looked overseas, whereas the opening up of the sector has enabled more talent to stay back and contribute to India’s growing space ecosystem. The emergence of private space startups, including Skyroot, is creating new opportunities for young engineers within the country.
The Minister’s introductory address was followed by an hour-long interaction and panel discussion with students. The panel included Vice-Chancellor of Banaras Hindu University, Professor Chaturvedi; Dr Sunil Kumar from the ocean sciences; Dr Ekta, Department of Science & Technology; Dr Geeta, Department of Biotechnology; and Dr Jay Jaiswal from the space sector.
Dr Jitendra Singh said the expansion of the space sector represents a fundamental change in India’s scientific ecosystem. “The age of silos is over,” he said, stressing that government institutions, private industry, startups, academia and research institutions must work together to build capabilities that can compete globally. The opening of the sector has transformed space from a predominantly government-led domain into a wider ecosystem in which young professionals and private enterprises can participate.
The transformation is already visible in the growth of India’s space economy, which has reached around USD 9 billion and, if the present momentum continues, could reach USD 45-46 billion over the next 8-10 years, the Minister said. He attributed this expansion to opening the sector and bringing a wider range of stakeholders into India’s space journey.
Dr Jitendra Singh also told students that India’s space story is no longer limited to rockets and launch missions. Space technology is increasingly being used to make everyday life easier, including in infrastructure planning, project monitoring and disaster management. Indian satellites are also providing information to neighbouring countries such as Nepal, Bangladesh, Myanmar and Sri Lanka to help them prepare for floods and other disasters, he said.
Taking the students through India’s wider scientific transformation, the Minister said the last 12–13 years have been an “Era of Science” in India, with technology receiving high policy priority and being increasingly used to improve lives. He said India had the scientific talent and human resources for decades, but the enabling policy environment required to convert that potential into national capability has strengthened significantly in recent years.
The Minister cited the Deep Ocean Mission, Quantum Mission, Artificial Intelligence, Cyber Security and the Anusandhan National Research Foundation among the initiatives creating capabilities in emerging scientific fields. Referring to the Deep Ocean Mission, he said India is beginning to explore the enormous scientific and economic potential of its oceans, including resources that have remained largely unexplored.
On biotechnology, Dr Jitendra Singh referred to India’s dedicated policy framework focused on “Biotechnology for Economy, Environment and Employment”, the development of the world’s first DNA vaccine against COVID-19, and the Genome India initiative as examples of the country’s growing indigenous capabilities and preparation for an era of precision medicine.
Referring to Chandrayaan-3, the Minister said India has demonstrated its ability to undertake sophisticated space missions with remarkable cost efficiency. He said the country has moved beyond the earlier phase in which it largely followed developments elsewhere and is now moving alongside the world, with India already ahead in several areas.
Dr Jitendra Singh also referred to the opening of the nuclear sector to private participation and India’s target of 100 GW of nuclear energy capacity by 2047, with nuclear power emerging as an important clean-energy source for future requirements, including AI and data centres. He said the increased priority accorded to research is reflected in the rise in GERD from around 46,000–47,000 crore in 2013–14 to around 2–2.5 lakh crore.
Responding to students on Artificial Intelligence, Dr Jitendra Singh encouraged them to embrace the technology while retaining independent thinking and curiosity. “You have to be intelligent enough to use Artificial Intelligence,” he said, stressing that technology should strengthen human capability rather than replace the curiosity that drives scientific discovery. Dr Jitendra Singh said India’s scientific progress has created a new self-confidence, reflected in the country’s growing global standing and the opportunities now available to its youth. Recalling PM Sh Modi's message “We can do it,” he said India has moved from an era when the world experimented and India followed to one in which scientific developments are taking place in India alongside the rest of the world, with the country moving ahead in several fields.
The next phase, he said, will depend on sustained collaboration, greater opportunities for young talent and the continued conversion of scientific capability into innovation, economic opportunity and solutions for everyday life as India advances towards Viksit Bharat.

title: Union minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan inaugurated various new facilities of ICAR-IIAB in Ranchi through video conferencing
subtitle:
Shri Chouhan appreciates the efforts of scientists in taking technologies from “Lab to Land” 

Shri Chouhan highlights the importance of scientific agriculture, improved seeds, integrated farming, balanced nutrient management and location-specific agricultural technologies for Jharkhand

ICAR-IIAB organises Pre-Rabi Kisan Goshti for 1,500 Farmers
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                08 OCT 2026 8:37PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The ICAR–Indian Institute of Agricultural Biotechnology (ICAR-IIAB), Garhkhatanga, Ranchi, organized a Pre-Rabi Kisan Goshti-cum-Agricultural Input Distribution Programme under the Scheduled Caste Sub-Plan (SCSP) and Tribal Sub-Plan (TSP) on 8th October, 2026. The programme brought together around 1,500 farmers from Ranchi, Khunti, Gumla and Ramgarh districts to facilitate direct interaction between farmers, scientists and policymakers and to promote the adoption of scientific and sustainable agricultural practices.
On this occasion, the Union Minister of Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan inaugurated various new facilities of ICAR-IIAB through video conferencing. The facilities inaugurated included the Admin-cum-School Building, Birsa Munda Multipurpose Hall, Jaipal Singh Munda Sports Complex, NEXTGEN Breeding Facility and laid the foundation for a new Guest House facility at ICAR-IIAB worth Rs 119 Crore rupees.
In his address, Shri Chouhan highlighted the importance of scientific agriculture, improved seeds, integrated farming, balanced nutrient management and location-specific agricultural technologies for Jharkhand. He also appreciated the institute’s efforts towards taking research and technologies to farmers and called for sustained farmer awareness and field-level extension.
Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan highlighted the rich natural and traditional heritage of Jharkhand and described ICAR-IIAB as an important confluence of agricultural research, innovation and self-reliance. He emphasized that while traditional knowledge remains valuable, contemporary agricultural challenges require farmers to increasingly adopt scientific and technology-driven farming practices suited to local resources and agro-climatic conditions. He stressed the importance of ensuring timely availability of improved seeds and taking appropriate agricultural technologies from research institutions to farmers’ fields.
The Union Minister emphasized the importance of integrated farming, including vegetables, cereals and livestock, along with proper knowledge of balanced fertilizer use. He particularly stressed the need to protect farmers from fake seeds, counterfeit fertilizers and substandard pesticides. He also called for effective implementation of farmer welfare schemes and ensuring that their benefits reach every village. Highlighting the importance of preparing farmers for the forthcoming Rabi season, he appreciated the efforts of scientists in taking technologies from “Lab to Land” and urged them to undertake a nationwide Khet Bachao Abhiyan in the coming days.
Shri Bhagirath Choudhary, Union Minister of State for Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare, highlighted the central role of farmers in the country’s food security and development. He emphasized the adoption of modern agricultural technologies, value addition, stronger Farmer Producer Organisations and Krishi Vigyan Kendras, soil testing and balanced fertilizer use. He also encouraged farmers to experiment with natural farming on a part of their cultivated area and stressed the need to protect farmers from spurious seeds, counterfeit fertilizers and substandard pesticides. He called for effective implementation of farmer welfare schemes and stronger efforts to take agricultural technologies from Lab to Land.
Dr. M. L. Jat, Secretary, DARE and Director General, ICAR, highlighted the potential of eastern India for a new agricultural transformation and emphasized the importance of strengthening agricultural research and knowledge institutions in Jharkhand. He called for wider adoption of Rice-Fallow Intensification, location-specific crop and variety selection, improved livestock productivity and research addressing challenges such as acidic soils and phosphorus deficiency. He also stressed the importance of natural and organic farming and appropriate planning for the forthcoming Rabi season.
Addressing the programme, Dr. D. K. Yadav, Deputy Director General (Crop Science), ICAR, emphasized the need to align agricultural research with farmers’ requirements and ensure that technologies reach the last mile. He also highlighted the importance of student development, appropriate guidance and strengthening opportunities in agricultural research.
Earlier, Shri Bhagirath Choudhary, Union Minister of State for Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare, accompanied by Dr. M. L. Jat, Secretary, DARE and Director General, ICAR; Dr. D. K. Yadav, Deputy Director General (Crop Science), ICAR; Dr. Sujay Rakshit, Director, ICAR-IIAB; and Dr. Vijay Pal Bhadana, Joint Director (Research), ICAR-IIAB, visited various facilities of the institute. The visit included the Dairy Farm, Crop Research and Training Centre, NEXTGEN Breeding Facility and Integrated Farming System (IFS) Unit. At the Dairy Farm, the Minister was briefed on Embryo Transfer technology for genetic improvement of livestock. At the IFS Unit, the dignitaries interacted with farmers and were briefed on integrated farming, agricultural waste recycling and resource-efficient practices. The Minister also participated in a plantation drive and interacted with progressive farmers. An exhibition showcasing crop varieties, livestock and dairy technologies, research achievements, agricultural schemes and farmer-oriented innovations by ICAR institutes and Government agencies of Jharkhand was also organized.
The Kisan Goshti focused on Farmer Producer Organisations and opportunities in Jharkhand, ethno-veterinary medicines and dairy farming, fruit crop production technologies, Integrated Pest Management in Rabi crops, crop diversification and Integrated Farming Systems, organic and natural farming, livestock feeding management, and lac cultivation. Farmers interacted with scientists and technical experts and received practical guidance on improved agricultural and livestock practices. Various agricultural and livestock inputs, including Nano Urea, Nano DAP, mineral mixture, improved seed varieties, wheat, pea, mustard and vegetable seed kits, a milk can cooler, and high-yielding tomato and brinjal seed varieties, were distributed to participating farmers. Publications and technologies developed by ICAR institutes were also released on the occasion.
On the occasion, Dr. R. Ramani, former Officer on Special Duty; Dr. K. K. Sharma, former Director (In-charge); Dr. Tilak Raj Sharma, former Acting Director and Joint Director (Research); and Dr. Arunnava Patanayak, first regular Director, ICAR-IIAB, were honoured for their contributions to the institute.
The programme concluded with a vote of thanks proposed by Dr. Sujay Rakshit, Director, ICAR-IIAB, who expressed gratitude to the dignitaries, farmers, scientists, officials, staff, students and all stakeholders for their participation and support. The event reaffirmed ICAR-IIAB’s commitment to strengthening farmer–scientist–policy linkages and translating agricultural research and innovation into practical technologies for farmers of Jharkhand.

title: India Began Building Bridges When the World Was Building Walls: Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal
subtitle:

Shri Piyush Goyal Highlights Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s 25 Years of Uninterrupted Public Service

India’s FTAs Protect Sensitive Sectors While Opening Export and Investment Opportunities: Shri Piyush Goyal

Andhra Pradesh Emerging as a Sunrise State Through Technology-Driven Development and Governance: Shri Piyush Goyal
date:

content:
Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal today said that “India began building bridges when the world was building walls” while addressing the curtain raiser of the 31st CII Partnership Summit in New Delhi. He noted that India recorded USD 863 billion in exports last year and has set itself the target of achieving USD 1 trillion in exports in the current year. This would represent nearly 16 per cent growth in a year when international trade is expected to grow by only around 2.5 to 3 per cent, while the global economy remains vulnerable to shocks and global growth is expected to fall below 3 per cent.
Shri Goyal expressed confidence that India would achieve the USD 1 trillion export target, noting that the target has been set not merely by the government but by the people and businesses of India, including 63 million MSMEs, large and small industries, global capability centres and around 250,000 startups. He also said that the Reserve Bank of India had once again raised its growth projections for the current year and expressed confidence that India would continue to grow at over 7 per cent and remain the fastest-growing large economy.
The Minister attended the curtain raiser along with Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh Shri Chandrababu Naidu. The Partnership Summit will be held in Visakhapatnam on 12th and 13th November.
Urging countries to participate in the Summit, Shri Goyal said the event would provide an opportunity to look at the India story through the lens of growth, opportunity and partnership. He urged the distinguished guests to ensure that their countries send strong delegations to Visakhapatnam and participate in the various programmes, panels, discussions and formal and informal networking opportunities offered by the Partnership Summit.
He urged CII to establish FTA utilisation desks across every State Council to help MSMEs effectively use Free Trade Agreements, understand new market access opportunities and rules of origin, join delegations, participate in exhibitions and conferences, and showcase their products, technologies and offerings to global markets.
The Minister also highlighted the milestone of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi completing 25 years as head of government, beginning with his tenure as Chief Minister of Gujarat from 7th October 2001 and continuing as Prime Minister of India since 26th May 2014. He described this as 25 years of uninterrupted public service and an unblemished track record aimed at making India a truly powerful nation, restoring the glory India had once enjoyed and making India a developed nation by 2047.
Shri Goyal said the collective commitment of 1.4 billion Indians is being taken forward by the Prime Minister towards the mission of making India a developed nation by 2047 and fulfilling the dreams and aspirations of every child born in the country.
Recalling a shloka from Chapter 3, Verse 21 of the Bhagavad Gita, Shri Goyal said, “Whatever a great leader does, others follow. Whatever standard he sets, the world pursues.” He said the country is proud of the 25 years of seva, or service, led from the front by the Prime Minister.
He highlighted the Prime Minister’s focus on reaching the last mile in welfare and good governance, referring to the Jyotigram Yojana in Gujarat, which he said was the first effort at that point of time to take electricity to every home and every farm and ensure 24-hour uninterrupted power for industry to promote industrialisation.
Shri Goyal also referred to the JAM trinity of Jan Dhan, Aadhaar and Mobile, through which India strengthened the connect between people and government, and to Digital India, which enabled digital technology and digital connectivity across the length and breadth of India.
Referring to the 10th edition of the India Mobile Congress, Shri Goyal said Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi had recalled that the Digital India movement had resulted in savings of over Rs. 5 lakh crore, or over USD 55 billion, for the nation over the last 12 years.
The Minister said that the Prime Minister has consistently chosen reform over the easy path. He cited the introduction of GST to bring different tax systems across the country under one umbrella and the integration of regional power grids into one national grid as examples of this approach.
He said that despite the challenges posed by COVID-19 and the two wars with which the world is grappling, India has continued to remain the world’s fastest-growing large economy. He said Prime Minister Modi has understood the value of technology and demonstrated how technology can serve people at large, with the adoption of modern technology serving as the mainstay and backbone of his work over the last 25 years.
Shri Goyal said that India had earlier been defensive in its approach and hesitant to engage with the developed world, including being unwilling to open up the automobile sector and the country to new technologies. Today, he said, India engages with the world with the self-confidence of a nation on the move, bringing to the table technology, talent, competitiveness and greater market access for its goods and services.
He assured that every free trade agreement and other agreement entered into by India protects sensitive sectors, particularly Indian agriculture, fishermen and MSMEs, while opening up opportunities for exports of agricultural products, fisheries and marine products, high-precision items, engineering products and electronic products made by MSMEs. These agreements also open investment opportunities for countries and companies to come to India and participate in the growth of the world’s largest market.
Shri Goyal said India’s economy, currently around USD 4 trillion, has the potential to grow to USD 30 trillion by 2047. He highlighted India’s youthful and aspirational population and its desire for a better quality of life for itself and its families.
On technology, the Minister said India does not shy away from new-age technologies and adopts the best-of-class global technology developments. He said the country has moved beyond concerns that new technologies could lead to job losses and now has the courage of conviction that these technologies will create new opportunities for India’s talented youth.
He said India would leverage new technologies to offer its talent and skills to the world, improve efficiency and productivity, make Indian goods and services more competitive globally, and create opportunities for youth in areas including cyber security and applications built around emerging technologies. He expressed confidence that Indian industry and the people of India would leverage technological upgradation to the advantage of 1.4 billion Indians by opening newer opportunities in jobs, business and entrepreneurship.
The Minister emphasised that trust is a defining element of India’s engagement with the world. He said that during the COVID-19 pandemic, when the global economy was severely disrupted, India met every international commitment on time, whether relating to the supply of merchandise or provision of services. Even during the strictest lockdowns, export-oriented units continued serving customers while following social protocols and precautions, while broadband services were moved into people’s homes to ensure that services were not affected. Service Level Agreements signed with global companies were also respected and met.
Recalling the 2022 G20 Summit in Rome, Shri Goyal said global leaders had complimented Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi by describing India as a trusted partner of the globe. He also noted that India had recently seen credit rating upgrades from several credit rating agencies.
The Minister said Indian industry is focused on remaining ahead through cutting-edge technology, progressing on carbon mitigation towards sustainability goals and benefiting from labour reforms that enable industry to prosper while providing Indian labour with social security, good salaries, wages and amenities for a better lifestyle. He said the government is continuously working on ease of doing business measures, good governance and dialogue between industry and government to meet the aspirations and needs of industry and the exacting global standards that India is now willing to adopt and engage with.
Referring to the theme of the Partnership Summit, Shri Goyal said it closely resonates with the five T’s he had highlighted at the 2025 Summit in Visakhapatnam: Technology, Trust, Trade, Talent and Tradition. He said these five T’s reflect great partnerships and that trade, technology, trust and thought leadership are becoming defining features and core elements of India’s growth story.
Shri Goyal also highlighted the significance of the Partnership Summit as an occasion to celebrate India’s achievements, present India’s growth story to the world and build bridges with countries and delegations from around the world.
The Minister said India would stand by its friends through testing and difficult times, reflecting the Indian ethos of “Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam”, under which the world is viewed as one family.
Shri Goyal also complimented Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister Shri Nara Chandrababu Naidu for technology-driven development and governance in Andhra Pradesh. He described Andhra Pradesh as the “sunrise state” of the country and said that when the Central and State Governments work together as partners, the people progress and there is greater prosperity for the people of Andhra Pradesh.
Shri Goyal said Google’s first AI hub is coming up in Visakhapatnam, where the Partnership Summit will be held, while Amaravati is becoming a quantum valley. He said Shri Chandrababu Naidu continues to focus on ease of doing business to promote investments and growth in Andhra Pradesh and the well-being and welfare of every person in the State.
He described this as “Team India at its best”, with the Centre and State working together, the Central Government opening global markets through free trade agreements and other opportunities, and Andhra Pradesh converting these opportunities into factories, data centres and jobs. He said Andhra Pradesh and its people have made India proud through their achievements at home and across the world. Referring to the discussion on AI, quantum computing and the growing influence of technology, he highlighted the contribution of people from Andhra Pradesh across the world in their chosen professions and their abilities in numbers and science, technology and mathematics.
Shri Goyal concluded by saying that India today is aspirational, Indian business is confident and the country is commanding global respect.  He said the commitment of 1.4 billion people drives India and expressed confidence that the 31st edition of the Partnership Summit would be another milestone in India’s and Indian industry’s growth story as the country powers towards becoming a USD 30 trillion developed nation.

title: Union Minister of Communications Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia Inaugurates 3rd International Bharat 6G Symposium 2026
subtitle:
Bharat 6G Alliance Signs 5 MoUs and Unveils 9 White Papers on 6G Technology

Joint Report on the Progress of the New Delhi 6G Declaration Also Released
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                08 OCT 2026 9:32PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The 3rd International Bharat 6G Symposium 2026, being organised by the Bharat 6G Alliance (B6GA) at Yashobhoomi, Dwarka, New Delhi, was inaugurated today by Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia, Union Minister for Communications and Development of North Eastern Region, Government of India.
The Symposium brings together policymakers, global technology alliances, telecom operators, industry leaders, academia, research institutions and other stakeholders from across the world to advance collaboration towards the development of next-generation communication technologies and India’s 6G ambitions.
The inauguration marked a significant milestone in India’s journey towards building a globally competitive, indigenous and trusted 6G ecosystem, with the exchange of five new Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs) and the release of nine Working Group white papers by the Bharat 6G Alliance.
Five New MoUs to Strengthen Global and Industry Collaboration
During the inaugural ceremony, the Bharat 6G Alliance exchanged MoUs with:
GSMA
one6G Association
GTI Alliance Ltd
6G Industry Forum (6GIF)
VoICE
These collaborations further strengthen the Bharat 6G Alliance’s engagement with leading global and industry stakeholders and reinforce India’s commitment to international cooperation in research, innovation, standards, technology development and deployment for next-generation networks.
With these new collaborations, the Bharat 6G Alliance builds further upon its existing international and domestic partnerships. The Alliance already has 10 global and 2 domestic MoUs/MoI collaborations, taking its broader partnership network to 17 collaborations.
Nine New White Papers Released
The Bharat 6G Alliance also released nine Working Group white papers, reflecting the collective technical contributions of its industry, academia, research and technology ecosystem.
6G Technology Landscape Survey and Roadmap for R&D, Platforms and Trials in India
Integrated Sensing and Communication (ISAC) for 6G: Technologies, Architectures, Applications, and Future Directions
Fixed Wireless Access: Bharat’s Broadband Backbone from 5G to 6G
Role of Optical Technologies for 6G
A Perspective on IMT Spectrum Readiness towards 2030 and Beyond
Sustainable 6G: Designing Networks for a Carbon Net Zero Future
Cellular and WiFi Synergy: Global Pathways to Inclusive Connectivity
Captive Non-Public Network (CNPN)
Security for 6G
The publications address critical technological and policy dimensions of India’s 6G journey, including technology development and trials, spectrum readiness, sensing and communications, broadband connectivity, optical technologies, sustainability, enterprise networks, Wi-Fi–cellular convergence and security.
One-Year Progress on the New Delhi Declaration
A key highlight of the inaugural ceremony was the release of the Joint Report: “Progress towards the 6G Principles of the New Delhi Declaration: Actions, Outcomes and Outlook – First Edition, October 2026.”
The report marks the completion of one year since the New Delhi Declaration was endorsed at the International Bharat6G Symposium 2025 and captures the progress, actions and outcomes reported by the participating MoU partners towards advancing the principles articulated in the Declaration.
The New Delhi Declaration provides a common framework for advancing 6G as a secure, resilient, open, interoperable, inclusive and sustainable technology ecosystem, with emphasis on international collaboration in research, innovation and standardisation.
The progress report provides an important mechanism for taking stock of the collective efforts of the participating partners and identifying the outlook for continued cooperation towards the realisation of these principles.
India’s Growing Role in the Global 6G Ecosystem
The initiatives announced at the Symposium reaffirm the Bharat 6G Alliance’s role as a platform bringing together Indian and international stakeholders to shape the technological, standards and ecosystem dimensions of 6G.
The Alliance continues to facilitate collaboration across industry, academia, research institutions and government stakeholders, while supporting India’s participation in global standardisation, technology development, trials, intellectual property creation and international partnerships.
The release of the white papers, the expansion of the MoU network and the one-year progress report on the New Delhi Declaration collectively demonstrate the growing momentum of India’s engagement with the global 6G ecosystem.
The 3rd International Bharat 6G Symposium 2026, being held from 7–9 October 2026 at Yashobhoomi, Dwarka, New Delhi, features discussions on global 6G vision, standards and technology leadership, trials and testbeds, AI-native and sustainable networks, spectrum, industry applications and international cooperation.
The Bharat 6G Alliance will continue to work with its members and international partners towards building a secure, inclusive, sustainable and globally interoperable 6G ecosystem, strengthening India’s contribution to the global development of next-generation telecommunications.

title: Union Minister Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia Chairs CEO Round Table on the Future of Telecom at India Mobile Congress 2026
subtitle:
“India Moving Towards End-to-End Telecom Value Chain, Shaping the Rules, Equipment and Innovation”: Union Minister Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia

Telecom and Technology Leaders Explore New Frontiers in AI, Advanced Networks and Digital Innovation
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                08 OCT 2026 8:28PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister for Communications and Development of North Eastern Region, Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia, participated in a high-level CEO Round Table on The Sovereign Inflection & The Future of Telecom during the 10th edition of India Mobile Congress (IMC) 2026 at Yashobhoomi, New Delhi.
The leadership dialogue brought together senior representatives from the telecommunications, digital infrastructure, network equipment, technology and consulting sectors to deliberate on emerging opportunities and strategic priorities shaping the future of India’s telecom sector. The session was part of IMC 2026, organised under the theme “Scale Without Boundaries”
,
with a focus on translating innovation into scalable, resilient and globally relevant digital capabilities.
The Round Table witnessed the participation of senior industry leaders from leading telecom service providers, network equipment manufacturers, technology companies, digital infrastructure firms and industry advisory organisations. The discussions reflected strong industry engagement and focused on advancing telecom infrastructure, fostering innovation, strengthening indigenous capabilities and supporting the next phase of India’s digital growth. Shri Amit Agrawal, Secretary, Department of Telecommunications, also participated in the deliberations along with senior officials from the Department.
The discussions centred on the rapidly evolving telecom value chain and the convergence of Artificial Intelligence, cloud and compute, advanced connectivity, intelligent networks and next-generation communication technologies
.
The participants also deliberated on strengthening domestic capabilities, fostering innovation, building resilient digital infrastructure and creating an enabling policy environment to support sustained investment and technological advancement.
Shri Scindia also said “I think we have been meeting quite regularly and therefore this is not an annual meeting for any of us. But having said that, what has come out very clearly in this year's IMC is that we have achieved a lot in the last decade. Both in terms of coverage, penetration, affordability, inclusivity, innovation and really providing the foundational layer for a lot of application platforms to be innovated in our country. We are the second largest telecom market, we are the second largest mobile phone producer. Now end to end value chain is going to be produced in India thanks to the vision of our Prime Minister with 8-9 semiconductor fabs coming up in India. And therefore the fundamental inflection point today is going to be based on who writes the rules, who makes the equipment, who designs innovation, who builds the technology.”
Addressing the industry leadership, Shri Scindia emphasised the importance of a partnership-based approach between the Government and industry in shaping the next phase of India’s telecom journey. He underlined the role of the Department of Telecommunications as an enabler and facilitator in fostering an ecosystem in which all stakeholders could contribute to the growth and development of the sector.
The Minister highlighted that the telecom ecosystem encompassed network equipment and optical fibre manufacturers, telecom service providers, internet service providers, applications, platforms and emerging technologies such as Artificial Intelligence. He emphasised that the collective strength of these interconnected segments would play an important role in determining the future competitiveness and resilience of India’s digital economy. Importance of moving beyond connectivity towards technologies and digital infrastructure that created wider economic and social value. He highlighted India’s expanding digital ecosystem and the growing role of telecommunications as an enabling foundation for digital public infrastructure, emerging technologies, innovation and economic growth.
The Round Table provided an opportunity for industry leaders to share their perspectives on sectoral developments, technology adoption, investment opportunities and policy and regulatory priorities required to support the next phase of telecom growth. The interaction reflected the Government’s continued commitment to maintaining an open and constructive dialogue with industry and ensuring that policy frameworks remained responsive to technological and market developments.
The deliberations at the CEO Round Table reinforced the vision of “Scale Without Boundaries” by bringing the Government and industry together to shape a future-ready telecom ecosystem based on innovation, resilience, trusted infrastructure, indigenous capabilities and global competitiveness
.
The Department of Telecommunications reiterated its commitment to continued engagement with industry stakeholders, innovators, technology companies and other partners for the development of a robust and inclusive digital communications ecosystem and for strengthening India’s position as a global hub for telecom innovation and technology.

title: India Targets 10% of Global 6G Patents and Standards: Union Minister of State for Communications Dr Chandra Sekhar Pemmasani
subtitle:
Dr Pemmasani Calls for Development of Indian Alternatives to 10–20 Critical Imported Network Technologies

“The Last Decade Was Digital India; Our Goal Is to Make the Next Decade an Intelligent India”: Dr Chandra Sekhar Pemmasani

Union MoS pushes for advancing Quantum Communications, AI-Native Networks and Telecom Security
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                08 OCT 2026 8:01PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister of State for Communications and Rural Development, Dr Chandra Sekhar Pemmasani today, highlighted India's achievements in the telecom sector over the last five years and outlined priorities for the coming years while addressing telecom industry stakeholders.
The Minister of State while speaking at the session “Shaping the Intelligent Infrastructure for 6G: A Technology Leadership Dialogue, CTO Round Table” held on the sidelines of IMC 2026, underscored that India has connected more than a billion people, connected every district with 5G through almost 5.6 lakh Base Transceiver Stations (BTS), connected villages with 4G and developed its own indigenous 4G stack. He acknowledged the hard work of industry stakeholders in making these achievements possible.
Referring to the strengthening of the telecom sector over the last year, Dr Pemmasani stated that most of the rules under the Telecommunications Act, 2023 have now been notified. He said the objective is to create a regulatory framework that is simpler, technology-neutral and suited to the needs of the modern technology era. He also highlighted the BharatNet and 4G saturation projects aimed at taking high-speed fibre and connectivity to every village and every home.
The Minister of State further said that nearly 136 R&D projects, worth approximately ₹500 crore, have been funded under the Telecom Technology Development Fund (TTDF). These projects are working on 5G, 6G, quantum communications, non-terrestrial networks, advanced optical systems, indigenous core and telecom security. He also highlighted the 5G testbeds in academic institutions for students, researchers and startups to experiment and build.
Outlining the priorities ahead, Dr Pemmasani called for identifying 10–20 critical network technologies currently being imported and for developing Indian alternatives, particularly in component manufacturing, chipsets, radios, routers and optical systems.
Reiterating the objective of leading in 6G, the Minister of State highlighted the target of securing at least 10% of global 6G patents and standards. He called for major telecom operators to have measurable annual and quarterly targets for contributions to standards, standard-essential patents (SEPs) and university research, along with industry collaboration.
On quantum communications, he called for C-DOT to begin real operator trials, including quantum-safe encryption on critical links and Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) wherever economically justified, rather than leaving these technologies in research laboratories.
The Minister of State also emphasised moving from AI-assisted to AI-native networks. He called for greater focus on national security, equipment security, supply-chain security, fraud prevention and protection of critical telecom infrastructure.
Dr Pemmasani further exhorted close cooperation between government, operators, equipment manufacturers and technology companies. He invited industry stakeholders to present their wish lists, particularly areas requiring simplification and policy changes in line with technological developments.
“The last decade was Digital India. Our goal is to make the next decade an Intelligent India,” said Dr. Chandra Sekhar Pemmasani

Union Minister for Communications and Development of North Eastern Region Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia, in his address, emphasised the importance of sustained investment, stronger international cooperation and enabling policy frameworks to expand affordable and meaningful digital connectivity.
“Scale Without Boundaries is not merely about expanding telecommunications networks; it is about expanding human opportunity. The next billion people we connect will be the hardest to reach, but they will also be the most transformative by bringing new learners, entrepreneurs, innovators and creators into the global digital economy. India’s experience demonstrates that connectivity can be scaled with affordability, innovation and public purpose. As we look towards 5G-Advanced, 6G, satellite networks and AI, our shared responsibility is to ensure that geography, income or circumstance never becomes a barrier to opportunity. Our goal must be connectivity without boundaries and, ultimately, opportunity without boundaries.”
said Shri Scindia.
The programme provided a platform for discussions on policy, regulation, investment and international cooperation, with a focus on advancing affordable, reliable, resilient and inclusive digital connectivity and strengthening the foundations of the global digital economy.

Focus on the Next Billion Digital Connections

Participants deliberated on approaches to mobilise investment, strengthen enabling policy frameworks and expand affordable and meaningful connectivity, particularly as emerging technologies continue to transform the global communications landscape.
The Ministerial Programme also underscored the importance of future-ready and resilient networks, international standards, innovation and strategic partnerships in advancing digital connectivity towards 2030.
Strengthening Global Partnerships for Inclusive Digital Growth
The deliberations reaffirmed the importance of coordinated efforts to ensure that the benefits of next-generation digital technologies reach a wider population. Participants emphasised the need for stronger international cooperation and partnerships to create an enabling environment for investment, innovation and sustainable digital development.
The programme reinforced the vision of “Scale Without Boundaries”, highlighting the role of technology, investment and international collaboration in advancing a more connected, inclusive and digitally empowered future.
For the Department of Telecommunications, the Ministerial Programme served as an important platform for bringing together global perspectives on the future of connectivity and identifying shared priorities for expanding digital access and strengthening resilient digital infrastructure.
The programme at IMC 2026 reaffirmed the collective commitment to advancing inclusive, affordable, reliable and meaningful connectivity, while fostering partnerships that can help connect the next billion people and support a more digitally empowered world.
