title: Department of Telecommunications hosts High-Level Roundtable with State IT Ministers and Secretaries to Accelerate Digital Connectivity and Infrastructure Rollout
subtitle:
Roundtable chaired by Union Minister Shri Jyotiraditya Scindia along with Minister of State Dr. Chandra Sekhar Pemmasani

“To realize Viksit Bharat @2047, we must act as Team India by accelerating Right of Way approvals, pushing BharatNet and 4G saturation to the last mile”: Shri Scindia to State Ministers

Centre, States/UTs Reaffirm Commitment to Faster Telecom Infrastructure Deployment and Citizen-Centric Digital Services

State Government IT Ministers and Secretaries discussed RoW Reforms, BharatNet, 4G Connectivity and Digital Inclusion at IMC 2026 Roundtable
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                08 OCT 2026 5:40PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Department of Telecommunications (DoT), Ministry of Communications, organised a high-level Roundtable Conference with State Government IT Ministers and Secretaries on the sidelines of the India Mobile Congress (IMC) 2026. The Roundtable was chaired by Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia, Union Minister for Communications and Development of North Eastern Region, along with Dr. Chandra Sekhar Pemmasani, Union Minister of State for Communications & Rural Development, and Shri Amit Agrawal, Secretary, Department of Telecommunications.
The Roundtable provided a platform for structured dialogue and coordination between the Centre, States and Union Territories (UTs) on key issues concerning telecommunications, digital infrastructure and citizen-centric digital services. In line with the theme of IMC 2026, “Scale Without Boundaries”, the discussions focused on scaling digital connectivity, accelerating infrastructure deployment and strengthening Centre–State cooperation to support India’s digital transformation and the vision of Viksit Bharat by 2047.
Addressing the meeting, Union Minister for Communications and Development of North Eastern Region Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia said, "Telecom may be a Union subject, but digital infrastructure is built on State soil
making our States true co-owners in driving National Broadband Mission 2.0. To realize Viksit Bharat @2047, we must act as Team India
by
accelerating Right of Way approvals to unlock SASCI capital incentives, pushing BharatNet and 4G saturation to the last mile, securing networks through Sanchar Saathi, and scaling Samriddh Gram so that connectivity meaningfully transforms every citizen's life."
The discussions highlighted the crucial role played by States and UTs in the successful rollout of digital communication infrastructure, particularly in addressing ground-level requirements such as Right of Way (RoW), land allocation and site access.
A key focus of the Roundtable was the implementation of the Telecommunication (Right of Way) Rules, 2024, notified by DoT under the Telecommunications Act, 2023. The Rules, which came into effect from January 1, 2025, established a uniform and transparent framework for telecom infrastructure deployment, including rationalised RoW charges and time-bound processing of applications. The Rules provide timelines of 67 days for general RoW applications and 7 days for Special Projects such as BharatNet.
It was noted that 34 States/UTs had issued Government Orders or notifications directing local bodies and line departments to follow the DoT’s RoW Rules, 2024. All 36 States/UTs
are live on
the Central RoW Portal. The Special Assistance for Capital Investment (SASCI) Scheme 2026–27, with an earmarked allocation of ₹4,000 crore, was also highlighted as an important enabler for strengthening implementation of RoW reforms by States and their agencies, including State PSUs, corporations and Urban Local Bodies.
The Roundtable also reviewed progress under the Amended BharatNet Programme (ABP) and the 4G Saturation Project. The ABP
is
aimed at upgrading the existing BharatNet network, creating incremental network infrastructure for new Gram Panchayats (GPs), connecting non-GP villages on demand and providing 1.5 crore fibre internet connections. As of August 2026, 55,780 km of Optical Fibre Cable had been laid and 28,700 Gram Panchayats had been upgraded and connected under ABP.
The meeting further highlighted the Government’s efforts to extend mobile connectivity to remote and uncovered areas through projects funded by the Digital Bharat Nidhi (DBN). These initiatives were aimed at bridging the digital divide and providing 4G connectivity to villages where telecom service providers had not expanded networks due to commercial considerations. As of August 31, 2026, 25,367 mobile towers had been commissioned, covering 35,771 villages/locations across the country. The indigenous 4G stack has been used in the 4G Saturation Project implemented by BSNL.
The Roundtable also discussed the Sanchar Saathi initiative and the importance of strengthening coordination between DoT, State/UT Governments, Law Enforcement Agencies, Telecom Service Providers and other stakeholders to combat cybercrime and financial fraud. Sanchar Saathi enables citizens to report suspected fraudulent communications, check mobile connections issued in their name, report unauthorised connections, and block, report and trace lost or stolen mobile devices. The Digital Intelligence Platform (DIP) was also highlighted as an important mechanism for intelligence sharing and coordinated action against cyber fraud.
Another key initiative discussed was the Samriddh Gram Phygital Services Initiative, an integrated service delivery model aimed at translating reliable broadband connectivity into meaningful, citizen-centric services and opportunities in rural communities. Through Samriddhi Kendras, the initiative brings together services such as tele-consultations and diagnostics, digital classrooms and skilling, e-governance, banking, soil testing, drone-based agricultural services, employment opportunities and e-commerce under one roof. The model was being piloted in Umri in Madhya Pradesh, Chaurawala in Uttar Pradesh and Narakoduru in Andhra Pradesh and has been recognised globally as the winner of the WSIS Prizes 2026 under Action Line C6 – Enabling Environment.
The Roundtable concluded with a shared commitment among the Centre, States/UTs and the telecom industry to strengthen coordination, accelerate digital infrastructure deployment, facilitate adoption of emerging technologies and expand citizen-centric digital services. The discussions reaffirmed the collective resolve to build a digitally empowered and connected India and advance the vision of Viksit Bharat by 2047.

“Our Aim Is Clear: To Connect 1 Billion 5G Users by 2030 and Lead Global Digital Innovation”: Union Minister Shri Jyotiraditya Scindia
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                08 OCT 2026 4:53PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi today inaugurated the 10th edition of India Mobile Congress (IMC) 2026, Asia’s leading digital technology and telecommunications forum, at Yashobhoomi, New Delhi. The event brings together policymakers, global technology leaders, telecom operators, innovators, startups, investors, academia and international stakeholders to shape the future of digital connectivity and emerging technologies.
The event is being organised jointly by the Department of Telecommunications (DoT), Ministry of Communications, and the Cellular Operators Association of India (COAI) under the overarching theme “Scale Without Boundaries”, reflecting India’s ambition to take digital innovation, connectivity and technology-led growth beyond traditional boundaries.
Union Minister for Communications and Development of North Eastern Region Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia and Minister of State for Communications and Rural Development Dr. Chandra Sekhar Pemmasani were among the dignitaries present on the occasion.
Addressing the gathering, Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi emphasised the transformative role of technology and the importance of innovation, connectivity and digital solutions in driving inclusive and sustainable development.
The Prime Minister also said “I would like to thank and welcome all the representatives of telecom operators, industrial leaders, experts, academia or startups all across the world to India. India Mobile Congress is the testament of India’s evolving telecom sector and digital connectivity. In 2022, we launched 5G from this platform. In 2023, I explained how India transformed from 5G rollout to 5G reachout and today, we are witnessing how 5G has reached every district of our country. Today, India has 5,50,000 5G Base Stations and mobile internet speed from 2022, has increased by 10 times. The revolution that has taken place in the telecom sector has directly benefited the citizens of India. Today, hundreds of government services are available through mobile phones. Government assistance is now reaching beneficiaries directly through their bank accounts. Through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT), nearly ₹50 lakh crore has been transferred directly to beneficiaries and credited to their bank accounts. This is not a small figure. It has also helped prevent nearly ₹5 lakh crore from reaching the wrong hands.”
The Prime Minister emphasized “Over the years, India has transformed from being a consumer to a creator. Now, the country is moving towards a stage where product design will also take place in India. The technology and intellectual property (IP) behind these products will also be Indian. All necessary incentives are being provided, and all essential reforms are being implemented to achieve this. In short, the 'Reform Express' is speeding ahead in the telecom sector as well.”
India Mobile Congress has an important role in transforming Indian telecom sector
Addressing the gathering at 10th edition of India Mobile Congress, Union Minister Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia highlighted India's rapidly expanding telecom ecosystem and the growing capabilities of Indian companies, startups and innovators in developing globally competitive technology solutions.
Shri Scindia said, “The decade-long journey of the India Mobile Congress serves as the table of contents for India's digital transformation story. When IMC was launched in 2017 with the theme 'Connecting the Next Billion,' the nation faced an immense challenge. Today, we have built a thriving ecosystem with over 1.35 billion telecom subscribers and more than 1.09 billion broadband connections. 10 years ago, 0.26 GB was the average Indian’s monthly data consumption. Today, it is over 36 GB, with data costs down 97%. Every drop in cost, every jump in usage has expanded the canvas on which an Indian can connect, create and innovate. Even during the unprecedented disruption of the pandemic in 2020 and 2021, telecom networks kept the country moving, serving as classrooms for our children, clinics for our patients, and marketplaces for our businesses. Since the Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi launched 5G at IMC in October 2022, India’s rollout has set a global benchmark for scale, reaching 550 million users across 99.9% of our districts. Our aim now is clear: to connect 1 billion 5G users by 2030 and lead the next era of global digital innovation.”
Shri Scindia further emphasized “IMC 2026 will witness the digital capabilities of our nations, The  demonstrations  you  will  see  shortly  showcase  the  depth  and  strength of  India’s  deep-tech  ecosystem-  from  satellite  connectivity  to  life-saving  cell  broadcast,  AI-native  pre-6G  networks,  sovereign cloud, terahertz communications and integrated sensing and communication.”
Highlighting the journey of last 12 years, Shri Scindia said “One GB of data would cost Rs. 268   in 2014. Today, twelve years later, one GB of data costs only eight rupees.”
India Mobile Congress 2026: Scaling India’s Digital Transformation
The 10th edition of IMC marks a significant milestone in India's journey towards becoming a global hub for telecommunications, digital innovation and technology development.
With the theme “Scale Without Boundaries,” IMC 2026 focuses on taking innovations from laboratories and pilot projects to widespread deployment and real-world applications. The theme reflects India's vision of building a digitally empowered, secure and growth-oriented ecosystem where technology can reach every sector, region and community.
The four key pillars of IMC 2026
Srishti
– Building the Future
: Promoting innovation, emerging technologies and next-generation digital infrastructure.
Samvardhan
– Fueling Growth
: Accelerating investment, entrepreneurship, manufacturing and industry-led growth.
Sashakt
– Expanding Opportunities
: Leveraging digital technologies to create opportunities for citizens, enterprises and communities.
Suraksha
– Strengthening Trust
: Building secure, resilient and trusted digital networks and technology ecosystems.
The event is witnessing participation from over 100 countries, further strengthening India's position as an important global platform for dialogue, collaboration and innovation in telecommunications and digital technologies.
The Union Ministers Shri Scindia and Dr. Pemmasani also visited the exhibition area and witnessed technology demonstrations showcasing India's growing capabilities across telecommunications, artificial intelligence, next-generation networks and emerging technology domains.
During his visit, the Union Minister visited technology stalls of leading companies and reviewed demonstrations of emerging telecom technologies and products. The Union Minister also interacted with participating innovators and industry representatives, encouraging continued collaboration between government, industry, startups and research institutions to accelerate the development and deployment of indigenous technologies.
DoT Showcases India’s Indigenous Telecom Capabilities
The Department of Telecommunications (DoT) is showcasing its vision of inclusive and technology-enabled development through its pavilion at India Mobile Congress (IMC) 2026, centred on the theme of “Samridh Gram”, an award winning initiative of DoT. Inaugurated by the Union Minister Shri Scindia, the pavilion highlights how telecom and digital technologies can empower rural communities and drive inclusive growth. It features glimpses of key citizen-centric and technology initiatives of DoT, including Sanchar Saathi, the Financial Fraud Risk Indicator (FRI) for strengthening digital financial safety, and initiatives of the Telecommunication Engineering Centre (TEC) and WMO, showcasing India’s capabilities in secure, innovative and future-ready telecommunications. The pavilion brings together these initiatives to demonstrate the transformative role of telecom connectivity in creating a digitally empowered, secure and prosperous India.
The DoT pavilion also provides visitors and international delegates an opportunity to understand India's policy initiatives, technology development programmes and institutional efforts aimed at building a resilient and future-ready telecom ecosystem.
New Telecom Products and Technologies Unveiled
The IMC 2026 platform also witnessed the launch and showcasing of new telecom products and technology solutions, highlighting the growing capabilities of India's telecom industry.
The launches demonstrate the increasing maturity of India's indigenous technology ecosystem and the potential of Indian companies and innovators to develop solutions for both domestic and international markets.
The Government's continued emphasis on research, innovation, product development, manufacturing and global partnerships is aimed at strengthening India's position in the global telecommunications value chain.
Focus on Next-Generation Technologies
IMC 2026 provides a major platform for discussions and demonstrations around emerging technologies that are expected to shape the next phase of India's digital transformation. IMC 2026 is also expanding the technology conversation beyond conventional telecommunications, with dedicated focus on emerging application areas such as Smart Mobility, Stadium Experiences, Industrial Robotics and Transport Technology.
Strengthening Global Collaboration and Investment
IMC 2026 is also serving as a platform for international collaboration, strategic partnerships and investment opportunities in India's rapidly expanding digital technology ecosystem. The participation of global technology companies, policymakers, investors, startups and research institutions is expected to facilitate knowledge exchange, technology partnerships and new avenues for investment and innovation.
The Government's vision is to build an ecosystem where industry, academia, startups, investors and policymakers work together to accelerate technology development and ensure that innovations can be deployed at scale.
The event is expected to witness over 1.5 lakh attendees, 500+ exhibitors and partners, 600+ startups, 900+ thought leaders, more than 2,000 technology use cases, 120+ sessions and around 700 investor meetings, according to the Department of Telecommunications' pre-event projections.
Towards a Secure, Inclusive and Globally Competitive Digital Future
The 10th edition of India Mobile Congress reinforces India's commitment to building a secure, inclusive, innovative and globally competitive digital ecosystem. Under the vision of “Scale Without Boundaries,” IMC 2026 seeks to move technology from experimentation to meaningful deployment, creating solutions that can address challenges across sectors and contribute to economic growth, social development and improved quality of life.
The event further strengthens India's role in shaping the global conversation around next-generation connectivity, digital innovation and emerging technologies, while advancing the country's vision of becoming a leading technology developer, manufacturer and exporter. With its focus on innovation, investment, inclusion and trust, IMC 2026 represents another significant step towards building a technology-enabled India and contributing to the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047.

title: India’s regulatory framework for satellite communication services is fair and non-discriminatory
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                08 OCT 2026 9:19AM by PIB Delhi
content:
A post is being circulated in social media regarding the fairness of India’s regulatory framework for satellite communication services and suggesting that it is being applied in a discriminatory manner. The Government has put in place a fair and non-discriminatory authorisation framework for all telecommunication services, including satellite  communication services. Under this, telecom licences have been granted to three Global Mobile Personal Communication by Satellite services based on non-geosynchronous satellite orbit based satellite communications, as part of its commitment to enable provision of satellite communication services in India. Under the terms and conditions of license, every such licensee is required to demonstrate compliance with security conditions. This is aimed at ensuring that services provided meet various security requirements to ensure safety of all users and their data. Security assessment as part of this process is currently under way in respect of all the three licensees. As and when this process is completed for a licensed entity, it may proceed to the next step of seeking assignment of spectrum. At present, all the three entities are at broadly the same regulatory stage. As such, the suggestion that the framework or its application is unfair or discriminatory is baseless and misconceived.

title: 9th National Review Workshop begins in Bastar, focusing on translating the vision of ‘Sahkar se Samriddhi’ into tangible grassroots outcomes
subtitle:
Guided by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s vision of ‘Sahkar se Samriddhi’ and under the leadership of Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah, emphasis on accelerating cooperative transformation, institutional strengthening and inclusive growth

Secretary, Ministry of Cooperation, Dr. Ashish Kumar Bhutani calls for strengthening democratic governance, transparency, accountability and good governance across cooperative institutions

Autonomy of cooperative banks must be accompanied by accountability and effective supervision; State Registrars must play a more proactive role: Dr. Bhutani

Recent amendment to the NCDC Act opens new avenues of financial assistance for institutions engaged in promoting cooperative development

States to be consulted on developing a common digital marketing platform for cooperative products and a model cooperative banking framework

Special focus on strengthening value chains in exports, organic products and seeds through national cooperative institutions NCEL, NCOL and BBSSL

Workshop reviews successful State-level initiatives and three-month action plans covering PACS, dairy cooperatives, cooperative banking, digitalisation and business diversification

Two-day Workshop emphasises developing practical models and future strategies for the cooperative sector through exchange of State experiences, challenges and innovations
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                08 OCT 2026 7:24PM by PIB Delhi
content:
In furtherance of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s vision of ‘Sahkar se Samriddhi’ and under the leadership of Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah, sustained efforts are being undertaken to make India’s cooperative sector stronger, more transparent, accountable and economically vibrant. As part of these efforts, the Ministry of Cooperation is organising the 9th National Review Workshop on 8–9 October 2026 in Bastar, Chhattisgarh, under the theme ‘Sahkar se Samriddhi — The Road Ahead: Scaling Impact through Cooperative Transformation’. The workshop aims to review progress under major cooperative initiatives, facilitate the exchange of successful practices and grassroots experiences among States, and develop outcome-oriented action plans for the next three months. The workshop brings together senior officials from various States, Registrars of Cooperative Societies, representatives of national cooperative institutions and federations, and key stakeholders from across the cooperative ecosystem. The two-day Workshop has been designed as an important platform for State-led deliberations and knowledge-sharing, with detailed discussions focusing on the revival of cooperative institutions, financial strengthening, business diversification, digitalisation, capacity building and improved market access.
Addressing the inaugural session, Secretary, Ministry of Cooperation, Dr. Ashish Kumar Bhutani said that the suggestion to organise this workshop on cooperative development in Bastar, a district that has long been affected by Left Wing Extremism, had come from Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah himself, making the initiative particularly significant and meaningful. He emphasised that the objective of the workshop was not merely to discuss various schemes and initiatives, but to translate the experiences and insights gained into concrete action on the ground. Stronger coordination among cooperative institutions, greater institutional collaboration and wider adoption of successful practices would further strengthen the cooperative movement, he said.
Underscoring the need to uphold democratic governance, transparency and the fundamental principles of cooperation at every level, Dr. Bhutani highlighted the vital role played by cooperative institutions in the economic empowerment of small businesses and ordinary citizens, particularly in rural and semi-urban areas. Referring to the cooperative banking sector, Dr. Bhutani said that cooperative banks serve as an important channel for delivering financial services to sections of society that often find it difficult to access adequate credit and other banking facilities from commercial and private banks. He stressed that institutional autonomy must go hand in hand with accountability and effective supervision.
Highlighting shortcomings in the administration and governance of cooperative banks, he called for a more systematic and strategic monitoring framework. He urged Registrars of Cooperative Societies across States to exercise greater vigilance and play a more proactive role in strengthening supervision. Weaknesses in oversight, he cautioned, could have consequences extending beyond individual institutions and adversely affect the credibility of the cooperative sector as a whole.
The Secretary said that the Ministry of Cooperation is working in close coordination with the Reserve Bank of India to strengthen the resource-mobilisation capabilities of cooperative banks and enhance opportunities for providing financial assistance at concessional rates to farmers and other stakeholders associated with the cooperative sector. He also emphasised the need to make cooperative banking more competitive through the adoption of modern technologies, stronger risk management practices and measures to enhance customer confidence.
Highlighting the importance of financial resources for cooperative development, Dr. Bhutani said that the participation of NABARD's team in the Workshop would provide an opportunity for meaningful deliberations on financing various schemes and institutions. He informed participants that a dedicated session with the National Cooperative Development Corporation (NCDC) had also been scheduled to examine the availability of financial assistance for cooperative initiatives and the specific requirements of States. He noted that NCDC has emerged as a major institution providing financial and institutional support to the cooperative sector over the past two to three years. Referring to the recent amendment to the NCDC Act, he said that it has paved the way for extending financial assistance even to institutions that are not themselves cooperatives but are engaged in promoting cooperative development. This could open new opportunities for various State-level institutions to access financial assistance directly from NCDC. He urged States to make effective use of these opportunities and pursue financing initiatives through stronger coordination.
Highlighting the potential of the dairy sector, Dr. Bhutani said that the workshop would hold detailed deliberations on initiatives undertaken by dairy institutions, opportunities for developing them into cooperative institutions and measures to strengthen associated value chains. Discussions would also cover human resource policies, institutional capacity building, innovation and the emerging requirements of the cooperative sector. The Cooperation Secretary urged all States to share new experiments, successful models and innovations being undertaken in their respective cooperative sectors. He observed that several noteworthy initiatives are being implemented across States, but information about these efforts does not always reach other States. Citing initiatives undertaken by some States in activities related to electric vehicles, he said that sharing such experiences would help build a strong national knowledge base of successful practices and encourage other States to undertake similar innovations.
Referring to the proposal to develop a common cooperative digital platform for more effective marketing of cooperative products and agricultural produce, Dr. Bhutani said that the workshop would examine the progress made under the initiative and the potential role of States in taking it forward. He informed participants that the Open Network for Digital Commerce (ONDC) had also offered its support for the initiative. He said that the Ministry would seek suggestions and guidance from States before proceeding further, with the objective of developing a practical and effective mechanism to connect cooperative institutions with wider markets.
Dr. Ashish Kumar Bhutani emphasised that the deliberations at the workshop had been designed to be more participatory, allowing the Ministry to listen closely to the experiences, concerns and suggestions of States. These inputs would help in developing practical models, guidelines and circulars suited to ground-level requirements. He encouraged States to openly raise challenges relating to the functioning, financing, administration and business expansion of cooperative institutions.
Highlighting the role of Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS) and tribal cooperative institutions, the Secretary Cooperation said that visits to selected cooperative institutions had also been included in the Workshop programme. These visits would provide participants with an opportunity to observe their functioning first-hand and understand practices being adopted at the local level. He stressed the need to link PACS and tribal cooperatives with State and national cooperative federations to improve market access for their products and produce and enable members to secure remunerative prices.
Calling for a closer assessment of government procurement activities undertaken through PACS, Dr. Bhutani said that States where PACS are involved in government procurement should undertake a detailed evaluation of their actual experiences. He urged States to share information on the commissions received by PACS, their real economic gains, delays in payments and the overall financial viability of such activities. He said that successful practices from different States could be consolidated into practical models for wider adoption across the country.
During the inaugural session, Chief Secretary of Chhattisgarh Shri Vikas Sheel welcomed representatives of all participating States and institutions and assured full support from the Government of Chhattisgarh for the development of the cooperative sector. He expressed confidence that the workshop in Bastar would provide fresh impetus to cooperation among States, the exchange of experiences and the development of practical solutions. He said that the suggestions and outcomes emerging from the Workshop would help advance efforts to make cooperative institutions stronger, more transparent, accountable and effective.
On the first day of the workshop, the achievements under major initiatives of the Ministry of Cooperation during the preceding three months were reviewed and progress against national priorities and action plans for the next three months were discussed in detail. These included the formation of multipurpose PACS, computerisation of PACS, the World's Largest Grain Storage Plan in the cooperative sector, business diversification, cooperative banking and initiatives associated with NCEL, NCOL, BBSSL and NCDC.
During the workshop, thematic sessions were held on ‘Cooperative Growth Story — North Eastern States and Eastern Frontier’ with special attention to cooperative development in Left Wing Extremism-affected districts of Chhattisgarh and Odisha, ‘Cooperative Banking sector and measures to strengthen credit delivery, promote business diversification, adopt new technologies, improve risk management and enhance customer confidence, empowering primary cooperative institutions through national cooperative institutions like National Cooperative Exports Limited (NCEL), National Cooperative Organics Limited (NCOL) and Bharatiya Beej Sahakari Samiti Limited (BBSSL). Discussions also covered strengthening the administrative and business capabilities of cooperative institutions, enhancing benefits for members and creating opportunities for sustainable development, emerging value chains through Multipurpose Primary Cooperatives (MPP) and Multipurpose Cooperative Committees (MCC).

title: From Regional Identity to Shared National Heritage
subtitle: PM Mementos brings local traditions and cultural expressions of Madhya Pradesh into a wider national space
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                08 OCT 2026 6:25PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The 22 mementos from Madhya Pradesh featured in the 8th edition of the PM Mementos e-Auction offer more than a collection of artworks, photographs and commemorative objects. Taken together, they form a visual map of the State’s living heritage, connecting traditions and historic places with indigenous artistic expression, ecological heritage, public institutions and symbols of India’s national identity.
The 22 mementos from Madhya Pradesh illustrate a central idea behind PM Mementos:
a gift may originate in a particular place, community or tradition, but its story can become part of a larger national cultural memory.
A State told through its places, people and traditions
The collection moves across the cultural landscape of Madhya Pradesh. From Ujjain and Khajuraho to Udayagiri, Maheshwar, Shajapur, Neemuch, Khandwa and the forests of Sanjay Tiger Reserve, the collection reflects the many layers of the State’s identity.
Among the notable mementos is a
small-scale metal model of Kandariya Mahadev Temple, Khajuraho
, which brings the architectural and sculptural legacy of one of Madhya Pradesh’s most celebrated heritage sites into a contemporary form. Another memento represents
Vishnu as Varaha from the Udayagiri Caves
, linking the present with the State’s ancient sculptural heritage.
The collection also carries the memory of individuals who contributed to India’s intellectual and social development. A statue of
Dr. Hari Singh Gour
, educationist, jurist and social reformer, represents the contribution of education and institution-building to the State’s public life.
A framed photograph of
Maheshwar Fort and its ghats
highlights the architecture of the State.
Heritage that continues to live
The collection also demonstrates that heritage is not confined to monuments inherited from the past. It continues to be expressed through the beliefs, artistic practices and landscapes of contemporary communities.
The
Gond Tree of Life paintings
are an important example. Rooted in the traditional Gond artistic vocabulary, the works bring indigenous visual expression into the national collection, demonstrating how community-based artistic traditions continue to find contemporary forms of expression.
The collection’s numerous representations of
Mahakaleshwar in Ujjain
, alongside depictions of Maa Rajarajeshwari of Shajapur, Mahamaya Bhadwa Mataji of Neemuch and Shri Dadaji Dhuniwale Mandir of Khandwa, similarly point to the continuing role of sacred traditions in the cultural life of the State.
From regional identity to a shared national story
The collection also moves beyond regional identity towards symbols of a wider Indian imagination.
A
wooden representation of the Lion Capital of Ashoka
, incorporating the Ashoka Chakra and other elements of the national emblem, connects Madhya Pradesh’s local expressions of craftsmanship with one of India’s most recognisable symbols of national identity. An
Atmanirbhar Bharat Jan Sampark Maha Abhiyan
commemorative poster, meanwhile, represents a more contemporary aspect of public life.
The PM Mementos initiative gives this journey a
public dimension
. A memento presented during a moment of public interaction begins as a personal expression of appreciation or local identity. Through the e-auction, it enters a wider public space, where citizens can engage with the object and the story it carries. Each object retains its local character while collectively contributing to a larger story of India’s shared cultural inheritance.
Since its inception, the PM Mementos e-Auction has made thousands of gifts presented to the Prime Minister available to the public, with proceeds dedicated to the Namami Gange Programme.
The auction is currently live and has been extended until 31 October 2026. Interested bidders can place their bids online through the official PM Mementos e-Auction portal:
https://pmmementos.gov.in

Paying tribute to the rich legacy of valour, professionalism and selfless service, he lauded the IAF for its sustained operational excellence and ability to employ air power decisively in an increasingly contested and technology-driven battle space. He said that the theme of this year’s Air Force Day- “Indian Airforce: Infallible, Impervious and Precise”- captured the true essence and ethos of the IAF.
The CDS outlined that from the skies of conflict to the skies of humanitarian assistance, the IAF has always demonstrated that air power is not merely about air combat, it is about national power, national resilience and national service. title: Indian Coast Guard conducts 12th National Maritime Search & Rescue Exercise (SAREX-2026) off Paradip coast in Odisha
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                08 OCT 2026 4:16PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Indian Coast Guard conducted the 12th National Maritime Search and Rescue Exercise (SAREX-2026) off Paradip, Odisha, under the aegis of the National Maritime Search and Rescue Board (NMSARB) on October 08, 2026. Under the theme “Leveraging Technology to Strengthen SAR Preparedness and Maritime Safety”, the exercise brought together maritime and aeronautical agencies to demonstrate operational readiness, interoperability and coordinated response to mass rescue operations at sea.
The exercise was reviewed by Director General Paramesh Sivamani, DG, ICG and witnessed participation from Coast Guard, Navy, Air Force, Shipping Corporation of India, Directorate General of Shipping, Fisheries, Customs, Marine Police, Paradip Port Authority, and Odisha State Administration. 32 observers from 30 countries also participated in the exercise, marking a significant step towards strengthening international cooperation in maritime Search and Rescue. Their participation facilitated exchange of best practices, enhanced global interoperability and reaffirmed India’s role as a dependable maritime Search and Rescue partner in the region.
The assets deployed included 15 Coast Guard ships, three Dornier aircraft, three Advance Light Helicopters, one Chetak helicopter, IAF C-130J and Mi-17 aircraft, two Indian Navy ships, along with civil and state resources and shore-based support units. The sea drill simulated a Mass Rescue Operation following a concurrent aeronautical and maritime distress emergency. As part of the scenario, a passenger aircraft carrying 228 persons ditched at sea near Paradip Port, with the fuselage impacting the container vessel MV Zumba, resulting in structural damage and fire. The exercise involved activation of the Incident Command Post, firefighting operations, helicopter evacuations, deployment of life rafts and air-droppable life rafts, Jason Cradle and Gemini recovery, rescue basket operations and scramble net procedures. The exercise also included a demonstration of Remotely Operated Vehicle (ROV) capability.
SAREX-2026 reaffirmed the collective resolve of India and its international partners to build a faster, technology-enabled and seamlessly coordinated Search and Rescue framework, in line with the vision of SAGAR and the spirit of MAHASAGAR. The exercise reinforced the principle that every distress call must receive a coordinated response and every effort must be made to save lives at sea.

title: Union Minister Shri Ashwini Vaishnaw Launches World Bank Group’s ‘World Development Report 2026: The Promise of Artificial Intelligence’ in New Delhi
subtitle:
Report sets out a framework for developing economies to harness AI for development through adoption, adaptation and advancement

IndiaAI Mission, MeitY and the World Bank Group jointly host the India launch; policymakers, development experts and technology leaders deliberate on scaling AI for inclusive development

High-level panel and State AI Showcase examine how India can move from isolated AI pilots to evidence-based scale-up across sectors
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                08 OCT 2026 6:04PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Shri Ashwini Vaishnaw, the Union Minister for Electronics and Information Technology, Railways, and Information and Broadcasting, today launched the World Bank Group’s
World Development Report 2026: The Promise of Artificial Intelligence
at an event held at The Oberoi, New Delhi. The Report examines the opportunities and challenges that Artificial Intelligence (AI) presents for developing economies, and sets out a framework for countries to harness AI for development through adoption, adaptation and advancement.
The launch was organised by the IndiaAI Mission, Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), Government of India, in collaboration with the World Bank Group. It brought together senior policymakers, global development experts, technology leaders and practitioners to deliberate on how India can maximise, and safely sustain, the development gains from AI. The programme also featured a State AI Showcase, in which States and innovators presented AI-enabled solutions from across the country.
The Report notes that AI can widen access to expertise, raise productivity and improve the delivery of services in developing economies. AI-enabled tools are already being deployed in medical screening, agricultural decision-making and education, extending scarce expertise to larger sections of the population. The Report further emphasises that these gains rest on strong foundations, including reliable electricity and connectivity, computing infrastructure, quality data, skills, education systems and capable institutions.
Shri Ashwini Vaishnaw, Union Minister of Electronics and IT delivered the keynote address and formally presented the Report. The Union Minister underlined India’s approach of democratising technology, so that the benefits of Artificial Intelligence reach citizens, enterprises and institutions across the country.
“AI is changing the lives of ordinary people. In Baramati, sugarcane yields rose by 40 per cent with 30 per cent less water and fertiliser, for farmers who have never used a computer  simply through voice on a phone. In healthcare, TB detection has increased by 35 per cent. Examples like these can change lives across the Global South and the world,” said Shri Ashwini Vaishnaw.
The Union Minister added that the Baramati initiative draws on satellite, IoT and weather data and has also lowered labour costs. In Gujarat, AgriStack is being used by 5 lakh farmers, and AI for animal health through Sarlaben is benefiting 3 crore cattle and their farmers.
India has emerged as a significant ecosystem for the development and deployment of AI, with applications in healthcare, agriculture, education, governance, financial services and other sectors of public and economic importance. Through the IndiaAI Mission, the Government of India is building a comprehensive AI ecosystem across seven pillars: IndiaAI Compute Capacity, IndiaAI Innovation Centre for indigenous foundation models, IndiaAI Datasets Platform (AIKosh), IndiaAI Application Development Initiative, IndiaAI FutureSkills, IndiaAI Startup Financing, and Safe & Trusted AI.
The Mission seeks to strengthen India’s capabilities across the AI value chain, while ensuring that AI development remains inclusive, responsible and suited to India’s scale, diversity and multilingual context. The Government’s approach focuses on democratising access to compute, data and models, addressing India-specific challenges, and creating economic and employment opportunities. Under the Safe & Trusted AI pillar, the Government is supporting the development of indigenous tools and frameworks for responsible AI, including AI bias mitigation, algorithm auditing, explainable AI, privacy-preserving AI and deepfake detection, and has put in place institutional mechanisms for AI governance and safety.
The India launch provided a platform for policymakers and practitioners to examine how successful AI pilots can be identified, evaluated and scaled to deliver measurable development outcomes, and how the risks from AI can be safeguarded against.
The event commenced with welcome remarks by Shri Sudeep Srivastava, Chief Operating Officer, IndiaAI Mission and Joint Secretary, MeitY, and Dr. Somik Lall, Director of Strategy, Development Economics, World Bank Group.
“One of the key messages of the World Development Report is not about creating artificial intelligence but deploying it. India has a unique opportunity to bring together institutions, markets and AI to transform millions of lives,” said Dr. Somik Lall.
Delivering the keynote lecture on “From AI Pilots to Scale: The Promise of AI in India”, Dr. Michael Kremer, Chief Economist and Senior Vice President, World Bank Group, highlighted that India’s progress in AI holds lessons for the wider developing world. “India’s huge strides in AI is not just addressing its own problems but broader development challenges for the world,” he said.
Illustrating examples from weather advisory for farmers and EdTech solutions in Andhra Pradesh, he said, “For the scale up of AI solutions, we need a full stack approach - not just elements of the software but humans and institutional elements that come along with it.”
Dr. Kremer cited India’s AI-based monsoon forecasting as an example for the world. The Government of India, through its meteorological agencies and the Ministry of Agriculture, tested and combined multiple AI models, including open-access models, and delivered the forecasts to millions of farmers through text, voice and AI-powered advisories. The model predicted the unusual 2025 monsoon, and Ethiopia is now following India’s lead. He said the case shows that where commercial incentives are weak but the social potential is high, government has an important role to play.
This was followed by a presentation of the key findings of the Report by Dr. Gaurav Nayyar, Director, World Development Report 2026.
“India is already approaching the path of AI for development by adapting tools to local contexts with the government playing the role of an enabler, user and regulator of this new technology. AI can solve for developing countries like India in decades, what could not have been done in a century,” said Dr. Nayyar.
The presentation set out the Report’s core messages for developing countries: be optimistic, be strategic and be pragmatic. Countries should adopt and adapt AI, then advance; focus on adapting AI tools to local contexts rather than spending billions of dollars building advanced systems from scratch; and make cost-conscious choices as enablers, users and regulators of AI. It also noted that the risk of job disruption is less imminent in developing countries, and that the countries with the most to gain from AI may be the least prepared, with only one of the world’s 25 low-income countries having published a national AI strategy.
Special remarks were delivered by Shri Neelkanth Mishra, Executive Director, World Bank Group, and Shri S. Krishnan, Secretary, MeitY.
“The World Development Report aligns closely with India’s AI roadmap  compute, data and models  and sets out a sensible approach to regulation: rely on existing laws and voluntary compliance, and revisit regulation as the technology evolves,” said Shri S. Krishnan.
Shri Krishnan said that human capabilities matter most, and that, in line with the Prime Minister’s vision, work is under way on an AI Talent Mission. He added that, with among the highest AI skill penetration in the world, India can support the Global South, while enterprise adoption of AI at home must expand, and that government must remain nimble and flexible.
A high-level panel discussion on “Making AI Work for Development in India” followed. It addressed three questions: the challenges of AI adoption in India, how India can leverage AI and adapt it to local contexts and needs, and the policies required to contain the risks arising from AI. The discussion emphasised that realising the benefits of AI will require policies that ensure its gains are widely shared and its risks are tightly contained.
The panel comprised Shri Neelkanth Mishra, Executive Director, World Bank Group; Dr. Somik Lall, Director of Strategy, Development Economics, World Bank Group; Dr. Vivek Raghavan, Co-Founder, Sarvam AI; Dr. Neeraj Agrawal, Chief Program Officer, Wadhwani AI; Shri Maneesh Singh, Vice President, BharatGen; and Shri Shankar Maruwada, Co-Founder and CEO, EkStep Foundation. The session was moderated by Ms. Shereen Bhan, Managing Editor, CNBC-TV18. The panellists stressed the need to move beyond isolated pilots towards evidence-based scale-up, strengthen local capabilities, improve access to data and compute, put in place appropriate institutional frameworks, and keep AI solutions relevant to India’s diverse social and economic contexts.
The panel discussion was followed by the State AI Showcase, “AI Innovations from Across India”, which offered a pan-India perspective on how States are deploying scalable AI applications across sectors to address local and development challenges. Each presenter highlighted one key AI-enabled solution, its implementation journey and measurable impact. The presentations were:
Navachetana
, an AI-enabled early screening initiative for children aged 0 to 6 years to detect developmental delays, presented by Shri M. Venugopal Reddy, Director, Women Development & Child Welfare Department, Andhra Pradesh;
MahaVISTAAR AI
, a connected platform for personalised advisories, digital services and farmer engagement, presented by Shri Fahim Shaikh, PoCRA Project, Maharashtra;
EdskGrid
, a GeoAI governance intelligence solution for education, presented by Ms. Richa Kulkarni, State Project Director, Samagra Shiksha Abhiyan and Director, School Education & Literacy, Meghalaya;
Vyuhaa-Cerviai
, a cervical cancer screening solution for the point of care, presented by Shri Dhritiman Mallick, Co-Founder and CEO, Vyuhaa Med Data, a winner of the NCG Catch Grant; and
The showcase highlighted diverse approaches, emerging models and solutions with potential for adaptation across geographies.
The deliberations underscored the importance of building public trust in AI, and of ensuring that the technology develops in a manner that is safe, responsible and inclusive. The India launch of the
World Development Report 2026: The Promise of Artificial Intelligence
adds an important voice to the global dialogue on harnessing AI as an enabler of development, and reinforced the need for countries to build the foundational capabilities, institutions and policy frameworks required to translate advances in AI into broad-based and sustainable development outcomes.
The event concluded with closing remarks by Shri Md. Y. Safirulla K., IAS, Director, IndiaAI Mission.

The National Biodiversity Authority (NBA) received Rs 9.68 crore from users of India's biological resources during the period from 01.04.2026 to 30.09.2026, in accordance with the Biological Diversity Act, 2002, as amended in 2023, and the ABS Regulations. Of the total receipts, Rs 9.56 crore was received towards access to biological resources from various sectors as given below.
Sector-wise Contributions
The Agri-seed sector accounted for the largest share of receipts, with Rs 7.16 crore, followed by Food & Beverages at Rs 1.59 crore and Animal Husbandry at Rs 62.01 lakh. Other significant ABS contributions included M/s Tata Chemicals Pvt Ltd (Rs 52.06 lakh), M/s Indena India Pvt Ltd (Rs 45.89 lakh), M/s Grow Indigo Ltd (Rs 45.79 lakh), M/s Novozymes South Asia (Rs 44.11 lakh), and M/s Nongwoo Seed India (Rs 40.53 lakh).

Diversity of Biological Resources

These include agricultural crops such as chickpea, red lentil, green moong, horse gram, flaxseed, guar gum, tapioca, buckwheat, brown rice, cauliflower, okra, hot pepper, brinjal and ridge gourd.
The biological resources also include medicinal plants such as Ashwagandha, Shatavari, Kalmegh, Vasaka, Licorice, Arjuna, Bacopa, Gotukola and Moringa, as well as soil microorganisms including Azospirillum, Azotobacter, Bacillus, Rhizobium, Trichoderma and Metarhizium. The range further includes livestock genetic resources such as Mithun (Bos frontalis), Jersey cattle (Bos taurus) and frozen semen of Murrah buffalo (Bubalus bubalis), as well as Red Sanders wood sourced from cultivated sources and auctioned material.
Linking Benefit Sharing with Biodiversity Conservation
Since 2008, the NBA has realised around Rs 278 crore through ABS and disbursed more than Rs 200 crore towards biodiversity conservation and benefits for communities, farmers, institutions and other benefit claimers across the country.
The ABS mechanism goes beyond monetary collection by linking the utilisation of biological resources with biodiversity conservation, sustainable use and equitable sharing of benefits. Funds disbursed through the State Biodiversity Boards and Union Territory Biodiversity Councils support conservation of biological resources, preparation and updation of People's Biodiversity Registers, strengthening of Biodiversity Management Committees, biodiversity research and documentation, and benefits to local communities and other benefit claimers.
The ABS mechanism provides a framework through which India is progressively translating the utilisation of its biological diversity into tangible outcomes for biodiversity conservation, sustainable use and benefit of local communities. The receipts generated during the period reflect the continued implementation of India's ABS framework and the fulfilment of benefit-sharing obligations by users of biological resources.

title: India calls for Flexibility, Pragmatism and Mutual Respect to secure Ambitious and Balanced Outcomes at upcoming UNFCCC COP31

ministry: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change

content:
India has called for greater flexibility, pragmatism and mutual respect among Parties to bridge remaining differences and secure ambitious and balanced outcomes at UNFCCC COP31. Speaking at the Plenary Discussion on Political Landing Zones and Outcomes at the Pre-COP31 meeting in Fiji, Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Shri Bhupender Yadav said the intensifying impacts of climate change demand moving beyond rhetoric towards implementation and convergence.
Addressed the Plenary on Political Landing Zones at Pre COP 31 in Nadi, Fiji.

Called for an ambitious and balanced outcome at COP 31, where higher ambition is matched by climate finance, technology transfer and capacity-building, and implementation respects nationally determined pathways.
— Bhupender Yadav (@byadavbjp)
October 8, 2026
Reflecting on discussions during the Pre-COP, Shri Yadav said that the shared ground among Parties was “far greater than our divisions”. He highlighted broad convergence on remaining collectively anchored to the aspirational goal of limiting global warming to 1.5°C; recognising that higher ambition requires proportionally higher commitments, particularly through scaled-up climate finance, technology transfer and capacity-building; and shifting the collective focus decisively towards implementation. India, he said, firmly believes that implementation must respect nationally determined pathways, allowing each country to transition according to its unique national circumstances and development imperatives.
The Minister stressed on the urgent need for innovative solutions and continued reforms to accelerate climate action. He stated that while global goals are shared, greater convergence is needed on approaches to achieving them. “The time has come to demonstrate flexibility on all sides,” he said, calling for optimisation of the tools already available under the Convention and the Paris Agreement. He highlighted the inclusion of Article 9.1 on the provisional agenda as a vital formal opportunity to address the matching of finance to country needs, while also emphasising the strategic use of Article 6 cooperative approaches to plug critical gaps in finance and other means of implementation and unlock market-driven resources for sustainable development.
Shri Yadav said India expects COP31 to chart a definitive way forward to enhance engagement, technical cooperation and targeted support for building capabilities. He stated that India stands ready for open and transparent dialogue to resolve these issues in the run-up to COP31 to ensure “a balanced, equitable, and historic outcome” for the global community, particularly the most vulnerable. He further emphasised that climate multilateralism can be strengthened at COP31 through an inclusive, consultative and consensus-based approach.
Concluding India's intervention, Shri Yadav said, “As we leave Fiji, our objective should be clear: to carry the constructive elements of these discussions into Antalya”. He added that the landing zone should be an outcome that is ambitious and balanced, advancing mitigation and adaptation while delivering the means of implementation that developing countries need. He reaffirmed India’s readiness to work with the Presidency, Chairs and all Parties towards this objective.
In the end, the Union Minister thanked Mr. Chris Bowen, President of Negotiations, for his efforts in ensuring open and engaging discussions during Pre-COP31, and extended best wishes to the COP31 President for the success of COP31. The Pre-COP is a preparatory meeting held a few weeks before the annual UN Climate Change Conference, which this year will be held in Antalya, Türkiye, in November.

GST Council recommends faster refunds to improve working capital for businesses

GST Council recommends measures for smoother movement of goods across states
