title: NHAI Releases Document on ‘Wildlife Mitigation Measures & Structures’ Highlighting Strengthened Wildlife Conservation Measures Along National Highways
subtitle:
Over Rs.19,700 crore invested in wildlife mitigation infrastructure and environmental safeguards in last five years

More than 2,150 wildlife mitigation structures have been constructed and/or proposed along National Highways across the country
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                08 OCT 2026 6:22PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Highlighting initiatives towards integrating wildlife conservation into National Highway planning, design, and implementation, National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) released a document on ‘
Wildlife Mitigation Measures & Structures
’ Commemorating ‘National Wildlife Week’ from 2nd - 8th October 2026.  The document was recently released by Shri Nitin Gadkari, Hon’ble Minister for Road Transport and Highways during
Chintan Shivir
held in Ekta Nagar, Gujarat.  The document reflects NHAI’s approach towards developing National Highway infrastructure that balances requirements of connectivity and mobility with environmental sustainability and wildlife conservation.
Over last five years, around Rs. 19,700 crores have been invested in wildlife mitigation infrastructure and related environmental protection measures across National Highway projects. These interventions are aimed at addressing key challenges associated with National Highway infrastructure development, including habitat fragmentation, barrier effects and wildlife–vehicle collisions, while maintaining safe movement of traffic.
NHAI’s mitigation planning is guided by the ecological sensitivity of project corridors, wildlife movement patterns and the technical feasibility of infrastructure design. This enables wildlife mitigation measures to be planned according to the specific ecological and engineering requirements of individual highway corridors.
More than 2,150 Wildlife Mitigation Structures
The document outlines a structured framework for wildlife mitigation planning incorporating both structural measures including underpasses, overpasses, culverts and canopy crossings as well as non-structural interventions like signage, fencing and speed regulation etc. More than 2,150 wildlife mitigation structures have been constructed and/or proposed along National Highways across the country. These also include Animal Under Passes (AUPs), bridge-integrated crossings such as major bridge-cum-AUPs and minor bridge-cum-AUPs, culverts adapted for faunal movement, canopy crossings and other specialised structures.
As part of the structural mitigation measures, around Rs. 4,600 crores have been invested in animal underpasses, Rs. 650 crores in animal overpasses, Rs. 8,300 crores in viaducts, Rs. 2,800 crores in tunnels, Rs. 2,500 crores in major bridges and Rs. 500 crores in minor bridges. These structures facilitate safe wildlife movement across highway corridors and help maintain ecological connectivity between habitats.
NHAI has complemented these structural measures with a range of non-structural interventions aimed at minimising disturbance and improving habitat conditions such as noise barriers, reptile crossings, rainwater harvesting and other wildlife management interventions.
Integrated Approach to Wildlife Protection
To guide wildlife towards designated crossing structures and reduce the possibility of animal–vehicle conflicts, guide fencing and noise barriers have been provided at over 300 km of National Highway alignments.
NHAI has also established monitoring mechanisms, including camera trapping, to assess wildlife movement patterns and support periodic evaluation of mitigation measures. Wildlife–vehicle collision hotspots are identified and appropriate measures, including speed-regulation boards and signages, are provided to minimise risks to wildlife as well as highway users.
Balancing Infrastructure Development with Ecological Conservation
Document also underscores the importance of collaboration between the conservation community and agencies involved in National Highway infrastructure development. The approach adopted by NHAI seeks to ensure that mitigation measures are incorporated at different stages of National Highway development, enabling infrastructure expansion to be undertaken with due regard to biodiversity conservation and statutory environmental compliance requirements. The detailed document is available on NHAI website at
https://nhai.gov.in/nhai/sites/default/files/mix_file/NHAI-Wildlife_Mitigation_Measures_and_Structures.pdf
Covering recent initiatives and project implementations, the document reflects NHAI's commitment to incorporate various environmental protection measures for National Highway infrastructure development. It will serve as a reference framework, documenting the range of mitigation measures and structures being adopted across National Highway projects.

title: Rural Development Ministry holds national level rural training centres meet
subtitle: Secretary Rural Development calls for a modernising courses, AI-Enabled Digital Transformation, Improving credit linkages
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                08 OCT 2026 7:33PM by PIB Delhi
content:
A two-day National Level Review Meeting of Rural Self Employment Training Institutes (RSETI) Stakeholders was organised by the
Ministry of Rural Development
at Shillong, Meghalaya. The meeting is being organised in association with the Government of Meghalaya and the National Academy of RSETI (NAR). RSETI is a flagship programme implemented through a three-way partnership between the Ministry of Rural Development (MoRD), State/UT Governments and sponsoring Banks, with a mandate to establish an RSETI in every district.
The meeting brought together senior officials of the Ministry, State Governments, State Rural Livelihood Missions (SRLMs), sponsoring banks, NAR and RSETI functionaries from across the country to review physical and financial progress at the mid-point of the financial year and chart a strategy for the remaining two quarters.
In his address, Shri Rohit Kansal, Secretary, described RSETI as a unique institutional model that brings together the Central Government, State Governments and the banking sector. He highlighted that, under this model, banks are directly involved not only in training and equipping rural youth but also in providing credit to enable them to establish sustainable livelihoods. He emphasised that the RSETI approach goes beyond conventional credit linkage and priority-sector lending, by creating an integrated ecosystem in which training, handholding, entrepreneurship and access to credit are brought together to support sustainable livelihood outcomes.
Noting the programme's national footprint of 647 RSETIs covering 634 districts since its inception in January 2009, the Secretary said around 64 lakh persons have been trained, about 72% settled, but the satisfying fact is that 46 lakhs of women in about 72% of total trained beneficiaries. He emphasised that training is a means to the end, and that the ultimate objective is sustainable livelihoods through wage employment, entrepreneurship or self-employment. He urged the sponsoring banks and SRLMs to undertake a detailed analysis of the credit-linkage gap among the remaining beneficiaries, including whether the gap is attributable to lack of demand from beneficiaries or deficiencies in credit delivery mechanisms.
The Secretary asked stakeholders to focus on five key priorities:
•        Improving credit linkages
•        Modernising and improving the courses offered
•        Improving the quality of trainers
•        Developing truly modern and model RSETIs
•        Achieving complete digital transformation and effective use of Artificial Intelligence
He observed that around 65% of trainees are concentrated in a set of courses, and called for a review of the course basket, including emerging sectors such as AI, digital and mobile technologies, automobiles and tourism. He also highlighted opportunities in the international labour market, such as nursing, caregiving, plumbing and foreign-language skills, and asked governing bodies to revise courses that have not been updated recently.
On mobilisation, he emphasised RSETI courses should be attractive enough that rural youth seek them out. He advised every State to commit to at least one Model RSETI, with a definite timeline, and called for the entire RSETI lifecycle, from mobilisation and registration to training, assessment, certification and outcome monitoring, to be integrated on the Kaushal Rural portal, with an AI layer to match candidate profiles with suitable courses and livelihood opportunities in India and abroad. Stressing accountability, he said, “What gets measured gets done,” and that performance will be reviewed by RSETI, with well-performing institutions recognised and rewarded. He urged participants to treat the programme not merely as a task but as a form of seva, and assured States that regular consultations would continue and genuine challenges would be addressed through reforms and simplified processes.
During the review meeting Shri S. Sasikumar, Joint Secretary (Rural Skills), MoRD, spoke on current updates and future plans. Describing RSETI as one of the country's longest-running and most successful skill development programmes, and a 100% centrally sponsored one, he highlighted its growing role as a convergence platform for training under various Government schemes.  He informed the participants that the Ministry is considering an expanded training portfolio including emerging technologies such as AI, Rural Business Incubation Centres, Enterprise Mentoring Cells, partnerships with local industries, a National RSETI Alumni Meet, common branding of trainees' products, structured post-training handholding and a model RSETI in each State.  Bank wise presentations were also made by the respective bankers, while State wise presentations were jointly delivered by the State Directors/State Controllers of RSETIs and the National Officers of SRLMs. The different sessions also covered the Ministry’s observations, discussions on best practices as well as targets for the remaining quarters of the current year and the next year. During the meeting, the RSETI beneficiaries, shared their success stories and experiences of how the training helped them become self-employed and build sustainable livelihoods.

, Sonowal proposed exploring a green shipping corridor linking Indian ports with Antwerp-Bruges. Both sides discussed green fuels, smart port technology, and dredging. VOC Port has signed an agreement with Port of Antwerp Port for training in capacity building in green shipping, and green fuel.
With
Lyonpo Chandra Bahadur Gurung, Minister of Infrastructure and Transport of Bhutan
, Sonowal highlighted National Waterway-2 and the Jogighopa terminal as Bhutan's gateway to global trade. The ministers discussed the potential of the Manas and Sankosh rivers, and the connectivity with the national waterways for improved cargo movement. Both the ministers
discussed maritime
training for Bhutanese youth at the Centre of Excellence in Dibrugarh which is being developed.
"Our talks with Saudi Arabia, Belgium and Bhutan show how India's maritime partnerships are growing across regions," said
Sarbananda Sonowal
. "With Saudi Arabia, we are exploring investment in ports, shipbuilding and resilient supply chains. With Belgium, we are working towards a green shipping corridor and smarter ports. With Bhutan, we are opening the Brahmaputra as a gateway for our neighbour to reach global markets and
build
skills for its youth. Under the leadership of our visionary Prime Minister Narendra Modi, India is a trusted partner for a connected, green and prosperous maritime future."
At The Future is Blue: The Next Maritime Generation and Ocean Changemakers: Women, Youth and India's Maritime Journey, Sarbananda Sonowal heard from young Indians and women about their aspirations for the sector. The session had the participation
of an all-women
tri-service sailing expedition which inspired the women cadets.
Indian seafarers have grown from 1.27 lakh to 3.23 lakh in twelve years, taking India from fifth place in 2015 to world's second-largest supplier of seafarers, with over 12% of the global workforce. Active women seafarers have risen from 1,599 in 2021 to 7,033 in 2025, supported by the Sagar Mein Samman initiative. India aims to raise that share through Mission 20% by 2030. Shipyard–ITI partnerships now provide 150 hours of on-the-job training, and a structured six-month onboard programme for GP Rating and Maritime Catering trainees bridges pre-sea training and life at sea.
"India's maritime future will be written by the youth," said
Sarbananda Sonowal
. “Today, our seafarers are trusted and respected on every ocean, and more women than ever are choosing careers at sea. Under the dynamic leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, we are building the skills, institutions and opportunities so that every young Indian who dreams of the sea can help lead the world's maritime economy."
Day 2 also featured plenaries on securing global trade chokepoints, the Global South at the maritime table, AI in maritime, green ports, equity in ocean futures, BRICS+ connectivity and green shipbuilding.
Union Minister of State of MoPSW, Shantanu Thakur
held bilateral meetings with Greece, Lithuania, Mozambique and Myanmar on the sidelines of Sagarmanthan 2026. Thakur held a bilateral meeting with
Stefanos Gkikas, Deputy Minister of Maritime Affairs and Insular Policy of the Hellenic Republic (Greece)
, on strengthening India–Greece maritime cooperation. With
Lithuania's Minister of Transport and Communications, Juras Taminskas
, the minister proposed a work plan for the MoU between Jawaharlal Nehru Port Authority and the Port of Klaipėda, and discussed direct shipping links and green port cooperation. With Mozambique's
Minister of Transport and Logistics, João Jorge Matlombe
, he offered India's expertise in ports, shipbuilding, ship repair and seafarer training. With
Myanmar's
Deputy Minister of Transport, U Tun Lu
, he discussed the next phase of Sittwe Port, cross-border inland water trade and maritime safety in the Bay of Bengal.
"From the Baltic to the Bay of Bengal, India is ready to share its strengths in ports, shipbuilding and seafarer skills so that
we can grow
together with our partners," said
Shantanu Thakur
. "Under the visionary leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, India has emerged as a trusted maritime partner for nations across regions. Through cooperation in green shipping, connectivity and capacity building, we are working towards safe, open and prosperous seas for all,” added
Thakur
.
Addressing a press conference at Sagarmanthan, Union Minister Sarbananda Sonowal said that under Prime Minister Narendra Modi, India has moved from maritime potential to maritime performance. The
Union Minister of State Shantanu Thakur
along with the
Secretary of MoPSW, Vijay Kumar
also accompanied the Union Minister during the press conference.
Over the last twelve years, port capacity has risen from 1,561 to 2,817 MTPA, cargo handled from 1,052 to 1,668 million tonnes and inland waterways cargo from 29 to 218 million tonnes, while median container vessel turnaround has fallen from 35 to 23 hours. He noted that Sagarmanthan has grown from 1,700+ delegates from 61 countries in 2024 to participation from more than 70 countries this year, including 10 visiting Ministers, and has produced 100+ publications that strengthen India's role as Vishwaguru for the global maritime order. Highlighting India's push to build green hydrogen, ammonia and methanol capacity so that Indian ports become green fuel bunkering hubs, in line with the Net Zero 2070 commitment, he called for turning dialogue into joint research, investment and technology partnerships. "India is ready to work with the world for safer seas, greener shipping and shared prosperity,"
Sonowal
said.

title: Ministry Of Social Justice & Empowerment To Hold Regional Review Meeting In Diu Tomorrow
subtitle: Meeting To Review Implementation Of Key Welfare, Social Empowerment And Social Defence Schemes With Focus On Last-Mile Delivery, Beneficiary Saturation And Outcome-Oriented Implementation
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                08 OCT 2026 5:51PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment, Government of India, will convene a
Regional Review Meeting (RRM)
in the Union Territory of Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu (DNH&DD), in Diu tomorrow to undertake a comprehensive review of the implementation of major welfare, social empowerment and social defence schemes in the Western Region of the country.
The meeting will bring together senior representatives from the States of
Rajasthan, Goa and Maharashtra
, along with senior officers of the Union Territory Administration of Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu.
Secretary, Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment,
Shri Sudhansh Pant
, will address the meeting and outline the key implementation priorities and objectives of the Regional Review Meeting.
Under the guidance of Hon'ble Administrator of UT of DNH&DD
Shri Praful Patel,
several senior officers are participating in the Regional Review Meeting. These include
Secretary, Social Welfare Department
,
Shri Ashish Mohan, Collector, Diu, Shri Rahul Dev Boora
and
Director-cum-Deputy Secretary, Social Welfare Department Shri Puneet Kulshreshtha.
Senior representatives from the participating States including
Shri Lalit Kumar, Director Department of Social Welfare, Government of Rajasthan; Shri Dipak Desai, Director Department of Social Welfare, Government of Goa; Ms Deepa Mudhol Mundhe, Commissioner, Department of Social Welfare, Government of Maharashtra and Ms Sonali Mule, Director under Government of Maharashtra
,
will participate in the deliberations.
Senior officers from the Ministry attending the Regional Review Meeting include
Additional Secretary
Smt. Debolina Thakur
, along with
Joint Secretaries Shri Sajeesh Kumar N.,  Shri Parveen Kumar Thind
,
Dr. Sandeep Rewaji Rathod, Deputy Director General
,
Smt. Pratima Gupta
and
Shri Gaurav Singh Rajawat, Director
, among other senior officers of the Ministry.
The Regional Review Meeting is aimed at strengthening institutional coordination between the Ministry, the participating States and the Union Territory Administration and ensuring
effective, transparent, accountable and outcome-oriented implementation
of social justice and empowerment programmes, with particular emphasis on
last-mile delivery, beneficiary coverage and saturation, efficient utilisation of resources and measurable outcomes
.
The meeting will provide an institutional platform for a scheme-wise assessment of progress, identification of implementation gaps and challenges, sharing of best practices and formulation of
time-bound corrective and follow-up measures
to improve the delivery of benefits to eligible beneficiaries.
Scheme-wise Review of Major Programmes
The Regional Review Meeting will undertake a detailed scheme-wise review of major programmes of the Department of Social Justice & Empowerment, including the
Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojana (PM-AJAY)
, measures for strengthening the enforcement machinery under the
Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955
and the
Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989
, and the
National Action Plan for Drug Demand Reduction (NAPDDR)
.
The review will assess
physical and financial progress, beneficiary coverage and saturation, utilisation of funds, institutional mechanisms, implementation of statutory safeguards, awareness and outreach measures, rehabilitation and social reintegration initiatives
, as well as convergence with the
Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan (NMBA)
.
A detailed discussion and open-house session will provide an opportunity to examine implementation challenges and identify practical solutions relating to
beneficiary identification and saturation, inter-departmental convergence, monitoring and data management, fund utilisation, grievance redressal and dissemination of best practices and replicable models
. The session will also focus on evolving time-bound corrective measures wherever required.
Review of Scholarships, Senior Citizen Welfare and NAMASTE
The day-long deliberations will also cover key welfare and social empowerment initiatives, including
Scholarship Schemes, Atal Vayo Abhyuday Yojana (AVYAY)
and the
National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem (NAMASTE)
.
The review of
Scholarship Schemes
will focus on beneficiary coverage, application and verification processes, timely disbursement of assistance, Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT)-related issues and measures to strengthen outreach among eligible students, particularly those who remain outside the existing coverage.
Under
AVYAY
, the review will assess initiatives relating to the welfare, protection and empowerment of senior citizens, including institutional care, active ageing, social security, accessibility, support services and convergence with programmes and interventions of the Union Territory Administration.
The review of
NAMASTE
will focus on the identification and profiling of sanitation workers and waste pickers, occupational safety and dignity, access to social security and health benefits, mechanisation of sanitation operations, capacity building, livelihood support and convergence with other welfare and social protection schemes.
Focus on Last-Mile Delivery and Measurable Outcomes
A dedicated
Outcome Review Session
will assess the extent of coverage and saturation of eligible beneficiaries, quality and timeliness of service delivery, implementation bottlenecks, awareness and outreach mechanisms, technology-enabled monitoring, grievance redressal and feedback systems, and convergence between Central Government schemes and programmes implemented by the States and Union Territory Administration.
Particular emphasis will be placed on
last-mile delivery and measurable outcomes
, with the objective of ensuring that government interventions translate into tangible improvements in the lives of intended beneficiaries.
The meeting will identify
priority interventions and specific action points
for the participating States and the Union Territory, with emphasis on strengthening implementation mechanisms, improving outreach, addressing gaps in beneficiary identification and ensuring timely and transparent delivery of benefits.
Way Forward
The concluding session will consolidate the key observations, priorities and recommendations emerging from the deliberations. The
Way Forward
will include finalisation of action points and responsibilities, strengthened coordination between the Ministry, States and Union Territory Administration, time-bound resolution of implementation issues, improved monitoring of physical and financial progress and submission of
follow-up Action Taken Reports (ATRs)
by the concerned authorities.
The Regional Review Meeting is expected to further strengthen the institutional framework for effective implementation of social justice, social empowerment and social defence programmes in the Western Region. It will also reinforce the Government's commitment to
inclusive development, social protection, dignity, equal opportunity and empowerment of vulnerable and disadvantaged sections of society
, with a continued focus on ensuring that the benefits of government schemes reach the last mile.

title: From Recovery to Renewed Livelihood
subtitle: Chennai, Tamil Nadu’s Nathan’s Journey towards a Stable and Healthy Life
date:

content:
Timely and sustained support through de-addiction and rehabilitation services can play an important role in helping individuals overcome substance dependence, regain stability and return to productive and independent lives. Counselling, medical treatment, peer support and structured follow-up can provide individuals with the necessary support to sustain recovery and rebuild their personal and professional lives.
Mr. Nathan, aged 34, (name changed)
from Chennai, Tamil Nadu, is a self-employed professional with an MBA degree. He received support through
Concern, a Drug De-Addiction Centre (DDAC)
, to overcome challenges associated with relapse and restore stability in his life.
The intervention included
regular counselling, medical treatment, spirituality-based support and participation in Alcoholics Anonymous (AA) meetings
. Continuous counselling, medicines and structured follow-up sessions helped him overcome relapse, develop a stable routine and strengthen his recovery.
With sustained support and his own determination, Mr. Nathan gradually regained control over his life. Regular participation in AA meetings, along with counselling and medical support, helped him maintain a healthier and more stable lifestyle.
Today, Mr. Nathan is happy, healthy and stable. He has restarted his company and regained financial stability, enabling him to support his family. He continues to attend follow-up sessions and AA meetings regularly, demonstrating his commitment to sustained recovery.
Mr Nathan expressed his joy and said,
"The continuous counselling, medical support and AA meetings helped me overcome relapse and regain stability in my life. I have restarted my company and am now able to support my family while continuing my recovery journey."
Mr. Nathan's journey demonstrates how timely intervention, continuous counselling, medical care, peer support and structured follow-up can help individuals overcome addiction, rebuild their lives and return to productive livelihoods. His experience reflects the importance of sustained rehabilitation support in promoting healthier, more stable and self-reliant lives.

title: NISD To Organise Five-Day Geriatric Care Training Programme In Diu Tomorrow
subtitle: Programme To Build Capacity Of Anganwadi Workers, Frontline Functionaries In Geriatric Care, Early Identification Of Care Needs And Referral Support To Strengthen Community-Based Support For Senior Citizens
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                08 OCT 2026 1:38PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The
National Institute of Social Defence (NISD)
, under the Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment, Government of India,
in collaboration with
the Office of the Collector, Diu, Union Territory Administration of Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu
, will organise a
Five-Day Geriatric Care Training Programme
in Diu District from tomorrow.
Secretary, Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment, Shri Sudhansh Pant, will inaugurate the training programme at Education Hub, Diu. He will also administer the
Pledge for Welfare of Senior Citizens
to the participants.
Director NISD, Shri Gaurav Singh Rajawat, will be coordinating the inaugural session. The Collector, Diu, Shri Rahul Dev Boora, will formally welcome the dignitaries and participants.
Around
50 Anganwadi Workers, frontline workers and grassroots-level functionaries
are expected to participate in the programme, which is aimed at strengthening community-based support systems for senior citizens and enhancing the capacity of personnel engaged in last-mile service delivery.
The initiative seeks to create a pool of
trained, sensitised and locally available frontline functionaries
capable of providing basic geriatric care, identifying emerging care requirements, facilitating access to appropriate Government schemes and services, and extending emotional and psychosocial support to senior citizens at the community level.
The programme assumes particular significance in view of the evolving needs of an ageing population, including senior citizens living alone, those requiring assistance with
Activities of Daily Living (ADLs)
and older persons with limited access to family-based care. The training will adopt a
practical, participatory and field-oriented approach
, enabling participants to translate the knowledge and skills acquired into effective support within their respective communities.
Focus on Holistic and Dignified Geriatric Care
The training will provide participants with an understanding of the
physical, psychological, emotional and social dimensions of ageing
, while equipping them with practical competencies for safe, dignified and compassionate care of older persons.
Key areas will include the ageing process and changing needs of senior citizens; rights, dignity and well-being of older persons; roles of families, communities and frontline caregivers; principles of basic geriatric care; assistance with routine activities and ADLs; personal hygiene; nutrition and hydration; medication-related support; mobility assistance; safe transfer techniques; fall prevention and home safety.
The programme will also cover
basic first aid and response to common emergencies, communication skills, psychosocial support, loneliness and social isolation, emotional well-being, and dementia awareness and basic caregiving approaches
.
Special emphasis will be placed on the
prevention, identification and reporting of neglect, abuse and exploitation of senior citizens
, while reinforcing the principles of privacy, dignity, respect and compassionate care.
Participants will also be oriented to
Government schemes, programmes, institutional mechanisms and support services available for senior citizens
, enabling them to facilitate timely access to relevant benefits and services.
Practical and Field-Oriented Training
The programme will combine
technical sessions, interactive lectures, demonstrations, practical exercises, case studies and field-oriented examples
. Group activities, experience-sharing and question-and-answer sessions will provide participants an opportunity to relate the training inputs to their field experience and develop practical responses to the diverse needs of older persons.
Practical exposure to basic caregiving techniques will form an important component of the programme, with emphasis on translating knowledge into effective community-level support.
The training has been suitably contextualised to address the
specific needs and circumstances of senior citizens in Diu District
, with a focus on strengthening locally available support systems.
Strengthening the Capacity of Frontline Functionaries
The programme will strengthen the ability of frontline functionaries to provide basic, safe and dignified geriatric care and support; understand the physical, psychological, emotional and social needs of senior citizens; assist older persons with routine activities and Activities of Daily Living; identify early signs of health, mobility, cognitive and psychosocial concerns and facilitate appropriate referral; promote prevention of falls, injuries, neglect, abuse and exploitation; provide appropriate communication and psychosocial support, particularly to senior citizens living alone or with limited family support; facilitate access to Government schemes and institutional support mechanisms; and strengthen coordination among frontline workers, the District Administration and relevant service providers.
Programme Coordination
Ms. Asha Sharma, Course Coordinator
, and
Ms. Ritu Dandriyal, Junior Consultant
, from the
Senior Citizen Division, NISD
, have been deputed to conduct the programme.
The
Deputy Director (Training) & Head, Senior Citizen Division, NISD
, is coordinating the programme in consultation with the
Office of the Collector, Diu
, and other concerned stakeholders for effective academic, administrative and logistical arrangements.
NISD has been undertaking capacity-building and training programmes in geriatric care and related areas as part of its continuing efforts to strengthen the availability of trained human resources for the care, welfare and protection of senior citizens.
Expected Outcomes
The programme is expected to create a pool of approximately
50 trained and sensitised frontline functionaries
in Diu District and enhance their capacity to provide basic care and support to older persons.
It is also expected to improve the
early identification of senior citizens requiring additional care or referral
, strengthen awareness of Government schemes and support mechanisms, and improve community-level support for elderly persons living alone or with limited family support.
The Five-Day Geriatric Care Training Programme represents a focused capacity-building intervention to strengthen the
local ecosystem of elderly care in Diu District
. By developing a locally available pool of trained and sensitised personnel, the initiative seeks to promote a more responsive, inclusive and supportive environment for senior citizens and contribute towards their
dignity, safety, independence, social inclusion and quality of life
.
The collaboration between the
NISD, Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment, Government of India
, and the
Union Territory Administration of Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu, through the Office of the Collector, Diu
, reflects a coordinated approach towards strengthening geriatric care and community-based support mechanisms at the grassroots level.

title: Union Minister of State Pabitra Margherita Inaugurates  State-of-the-Art Silkworm Seed Infrastructure at Jorhat, Assam
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                08 OCT 2026 5:15PM by PIB Delhi
content:
In a significant step towards modernising sericulture infrastructure and strengthening rural livelihoods in the North-Eastern Region, Union Minister of State for Textiles Pabitra Margherita inaugurated the newly constructed Grainage Building and Cold Storage facility at the CSB-Silkworm Seed Production Centre (SSPC), Rowriah, Jorhat in the august presence of Kamakhya Prasad Tasa, Member of Parliament (Kaziranga), Hitendra Nath Goswami, Member of Legislative Assembly (Jorhat), Dr. Dipjyoti Rajkhowa, Vice-Chancellor, Smt. Lakhimi Dutta, Director of Sericulture, Government of Assam, and P. Sivakumar, Member Secretary, Central Silk Board, other senior officials and heads of various organizations under the Ministry of Textiles.
Established under the North-East Region Textile Promotion Scheme (NERTPS), the state-of-the-art facility has an annual capacity to produce 30 lakh Disease-Free Layings (DFLs) of mulberry hybrid seed and preserve up to 1 crore DFLs. The infrastructure will help ensure timely availability of quality silkworm seed and enhance seed production efficiency in the region. The upgraded facility is expected to further strengthen the regional sericulture value chain, generate employment opportunities, and create business opportunities for local suppliers and traders, thereby contributing to the socio-economic development of sericulture farmers.
Addressing the gathering, Union Minister of State for Textiles, Pabitra Margherita emphasised that quality silkworm seed, modern infrastructure, technology and skill development are vital for a productive and sustainable sericulture sector, highlighted the Central Silk Board’s strong seed production network covering both mulberry and Vanya sectors. He noted that CSB-NSSO caters to the mulberry seed sector, while BTSSO and MESSO support the Vanya seed sector. Highlighting Assam’s rich silk heritage and the potential of the North-Eastern Region, that the State contributes approximately 84% (73 MT) of India’s Muga silk and 74% (2131 MT) of Eri silk production and recorded raw silk production of 6% (9 MT) of mulberry silk in  2026-27 (upto July). During the same period, the North-Eastern Region recorded 142 MT of mulberry silk, 3 MT of Tasar silk, 2890 MT of Eri silk and 87 MT of Muga silk, and these production trends further underline the significance of strengthening the sericulture ecosystem in Assam and the North-Eastern Region.  He underlined the sector’s significant livelihood potential, with sericulture estimated to generate employment for around 29.50 lakh persons during 2025-26, highlighting the region’s strong potential in Vanya silk production and its growing importance in India’s silk economy. And, he noted that initiatives such as Mission Senehjori can help transform Muga silk into a high-value global product. He stressed the importance of entrepreneurship and stakeholder collaboration to enhance farmers’ productivity, create rural livelihoods and strengthen the Aatmanirbhar North-East. He called for stronger collaboration among the Central Silk Board, State Government, research institutions, farmers, entrepreneurs and other stakeholders to contribute to the development of a Viksit Assam and, in turn, a Viksit Bharat.
As part of the programme, an interactive Seri-Stakeholder Meet was organised to facilitate engagement with stakeholders and deliberate on issues concerning the sericulture sector. Progressive sericulture farmers were felicitated, while P1 Disease-Free Layings were directly distributed to sericulture farmers. Certificates were also presented to trainees who successfully completed training under the Ministry of Textiles’ flagship Samarth Scheme, promoting skill development and capacity building in the textile and sericulture ecosystem.
The inauguration marks an important milestone in CSB’s efforts to strengthen the silkworm seed production ecosystem in Assam and the North-Eastern Region, supporting farmers with quality seed, modern infrastructure and improved livelihood opportunities.

National SC-ST Hub (NSSH)
is advancing inclusive entrepreneurship by enabling SC/ST enterprises to build capabilities and access wider market opportunities. Through interventions spanning finance, technology, training, mentoring and market linkages, the scheme addresses key barriers across the enterprise journey. Its focus on public procurement further connects SC/ST-owned MSEs with institutional buyers. With growing beneficiary reach, training support and procurement participation, NSSH is helping create a more competitive MSME ecosystem.
Building an Inclusive Entrepreneurship Ecosystem
Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) provide an important pathway to entrepreneurship, employment and economic opportunity across India’s urban and rural areas. Making these opportunities more inclusive requires enabling entrepreneurs from historically underrepresented communities to participate, compete and grow. In this context, promoting enterprise ownership among
Scheduled Caste (SC) and Scheduled Tribe (ST) communities
is an important priority. Greater access to finance, skills, technology and markets can help broaden their participation in India’s MSME ecosystem.
National SC-ST Hub: Enabling Enterprise Growth
Launched on
18 October 2016
, the
National SC-ST Hub (NSSH) Scheme
provides focused support to enterprises across different stages of their growth journey. Implemented through the
National Small Industries Corporation (NSIC)
, the scheme helps address barriers faced by SC/ST-owned enterprises and supports their participation in public procurement.
Enterprise development initiatives under NSSH include training, mentoring, business development, networking and knowledge support. Together, these interventions help entrepreneurs improve business capabilities, access new opportunities and build more competitive enterprises.
Expanding Reach, Deepening Inclusion
NSSH’s impact is reflected not only in the number of entrepreneurs supported, but also in their growing participation in markets. By linking entrepreneurial support with procurement opportunities, the scheme is helping SC/ST-owned businesses improve their capabilities, expand market presence and pursue sustainable growth.
Since its inception, NSSH has assisted
1,90,414 beneficiaries
, and
trained 54,499 candidates
, as of 31st July 2026. It has also contributed to a significant expansion in procurement from SC/ST Owned MSEs, which increased
nearly 39-fold from ₹99.37 crore in 2015-16 to ₹4,013.42 crore in 2025-26. Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu and Assam
emerged as the five leading States under NSSH.
During the period 2025-26:
₹4013.42 crore procurement
recorded from
12,524 MSEs
10,717 candidates trained
through
47 institutions across 27 States
, including
24 Aspirational Districts
55% of candidates trained were women
Training programmes were aligned with
public procurement and GeM opportunities
to improve their market relevance. Key areas included cafeteria management and food production, welding and Computer-Aided Design (CAD)/Computer-Aided Manufacturing (CAM), laundry services, fashion designing and tailoring and bamboo-based work.
Supporting Enterprises Across the Growth Journey
NSSH brings together a range of interventions to address different requirements of enterprise growth.
Special Credit Linked Capital Subsidy Scheme (SCLCSS)
SCLCSS supports new and existing SC/ST-owned MSEs in strengthening capacity through investment in plant, machinery and equipment. It provides a
25% capital subsidy, capped at ₹25 lakh
, for purchases financed through institutional credit. The scheme covers both manufacturing and service enterprises without product/sector-specific restrictions.
Progress since inception (2016) till March 2026:
3,160 MSEs
received support, amounting to
₹356.10 crore
Coverage extended to
233 districts across 27 States and UTs
Single Point Registration Scheme (SPRS)
SPRS helps MSEs access Government procurement opportunities through registration with NSIC. Registered MSEs receive
free tender sets and exemption from payment of Earnest Money Deposit (EMD)
, alongside other procurement benefits.
Under the Public Procurement Policy, Central Ministries, Departments and CPSEs are required to procure
25% of their annual purchases from MSEs
, with
4% of total procurement earmarked for SC/ST-owned MSEs
.
Special Marketing Assistance Scheme (SMAS)
SMAS helps SC/ST enterprises improve product visibility and competitiveness through exhibitions, trade fairs, vendor programmes, workshops and awareness campaigns. Registered enterprises can participate in
up to four domestic and two international events each financial year
.
International exhibition support extends up to
₹3 lakh for micro, ₹2.5 lakh for small and ₹1.5 lakh for medium enterprises
. Enterprises must be registered on the
Udyam Registration Portal and MSME Data Bank
.
Progress during 2025-26:
141 SC/ST MSEs
were facilitated to participate in
4 domestic exhibitions
247 Special Vendor Development Programmes
were organised with CPSEs
197 e-tendering workshops
were conducted
230 awareness workshops
were organised with Central Public Sector Enterprises (CPSEs) and Government departments
Bank Loan Processing Reimbursement Scheme
Designed to lower borrowing costs for SC/ST MSEs, the support reimburses
80% of loan processing fees or ₹1 lakh, whichever is lower
, excluding applicable taxes. Benefits can be claimed after loan disbursement and multiple times in a financial year. Loans from
Scheduled Commercial Banks, NBFCs and State Finance Corporations
are covered.
Bank Guarantee Charges Reimbursement Scheme
To ease the cost of participating in
Central or State Government and Public Sector Enterprise tenders
, SC/ST MSEs can claim reimbursement of Performance Bank Guarantee charges. The support covers
80% of eligible charges or ₹1 lakh, whichever is lower
, excluding applicable taxes.
Testing Fee Reimbursement Scheme
This scheme helps SC/ST MSEs reduce costs associated with product testing, licensing and certification given by
Bureau Of Indian Standards
. It reimburses
80% of eligible testing fees or ₹1 lakh, whichever is lower
, excluding applicable taxes in a financial year.
Testing must be undertaken through
NABL/BIS-accredited, Government or PSU laboratories
.
Export Promotion Council Membership Reimbursement Scheme
To facilitate access to export networks, SC/ST MSEs receive support towards membership of
Export Promotion Councils (EPCs)
. The reimbursement covers
80% of eligible membership charges or ₹20,000, whichever is lower
, excluding applicable taxes per financial year. It includes
annual membership fees, one-time subscription charges and entry fees
. Applicants must hold a valid
Import Export Code (IEC) and Registration-cum-Membership Certificate (RCMC)
.
Capacity Building Management Fee Reimbursement Scheme
Managerial and business skills are supported through short-term training at
the top 50 management institutes identified under NIRF
. SC/ST entrepreneurs and their wards can attend programmes lasting
1-30 days
, with up to two courses supported annually. Participants can receive
90% of course fees or ₹1 lakh, whichever is lower
, per financial year.
Membership Fee of Government-Promoted E-Commerce Portals
This component helps SC/ST MSEs expand digital market access through
Government-promoted e-commerce portals
. These include
GeM, e-Khadi, TRIFED, Tribes India and MSME Mart
. It reimburses
80% of membership fees or ₹25,000, whichever is lower
, excluding applicable taxes per financial year.
This integrated approach helps enterprises move from being potential suppliers to competitive participants in institutional and Government markets.
From Support to Market Success
Beyond financial and market-related assistance, NSSH helps enterprises translate business support into stronger commercial outcomes. The
Business Accelerator Programme (BAP)
provides structured mentorship and industry insights across business strategy, pricing, operational efficiency and market positioning.
The programme helps entrepreneurs adopt structured, data-driven approaches and align their businesses with market requirements. This strengthens their competitiveness and opens larger opportunities, particularly in
Government procurement
.
Success Stories (BAP)
Creating Relevance in Compliance-Driven Markets- M/s Safety & Security Engineering, West Bengal
Mr. Debasish Mondal strengthened pricing, cost management and market positioning. The support improved his enterprise’s competitiveness in Government procurement. It subsequently secured tenders worth ₹8.48 lakh from Power Grid Corporation of India Limited.
Scaling Clean Energy- M/s Renergy Solution Pvt. Ltd., Assam
Mr. Bhargav Deori strengthened business processes, strategic direction and market positioning for his renewable energy enterprise. The programme improved his enterprise’s engagement with procurement platforms and readiness for Government tenders. This enabled the enterprise to better leverage public procurement opportunities and expand its presence in the renewable energy sector.
Powering Motion with Precision-Sawalaram Enterprises, Maharashtra
Shri Sunil Popatrao Jagtap strengthened his business strategy and understanding of Government procurement. Applying these insights, Sawalaram Enterprises secured a ₹5.10 lakh SAIL tender for hydraulic cylinders. The opportunity strengthened business performance and expanded the enterprise’s market presence.
Strengthening Entrepreneurship, Advancing Inclusion
The National SC-ST Hub is widening opportunities for SC/ST entrepreneurs to participate more meaningfully in India’s economic growth. Its interventions help businesses build skills and connect with larger markets. This progress is also enabling greater participation in public procurement and creating pathways for employment and enterprise growth. As its reach expands, NSSH is contributing to a
more inclusive, diverse and competitive MSME ecosystem
.

title: NHRC, India concludes its two-day Bihar Open Hearing and Camp Sitting in Patna
subtitle:
More than 70 cases including bonded labour heard in the presence of complainants, victims and officers concerned

More than Rs 1 crore paid as relief to the victims on NHRC recommendations; more than Rs. 50 lakh as relief in other cases

Senior officers sensitised on the issues pertaining to crime against women, children and timely submission of reports

The Commission also interacted with the representatives of NGOs, civil society organisations and human rights defenders to strengthen coordination
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                08 OCT 2026 9:05PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC), India led by Chairperson, Justice V. Ramasubramanian today concluded its two-day Bihar Open Hearing and Camp sitting in Patna. The Chairperson and Members, Justice (Dr.) Bidyut Ranjan Sarangi and Smt. Vijaya Bharathi Sayani heard more than 70 alleged cases of human rights violations in the presence of victims and concerned officers. The State Chief Secretary, Shri Pratyaya Amrit and DGP, Ms. Preeta Verma, NHRC Secretary General, Shri Piyush Goyal, DG (I), Smt. Anupama Nilekar Chandra, Joint Secretary, Shri Samir Kumar and other senior officers were present.
On Day-1, the Commission heard 30 cases and closed 19 cases after hearing the parties and finding the recommendations complied with. The State submitted proof of payment in 10 cases as recommended by the Commission, thereby providing relief for victims and their families. Altogether, compensation exceeding Rs. 1 crore was reported as disbursed, marking a significant step in ensuring justice and redress for human rights violations.
Various cases of serious human rights violations were taken up. In a case pertaining to a woman victim, the Commission directed the Bihar DGP to provide her protection and a dedicated helpline number she can call in case of any threat or when in need. The DGP was further directed to constitute an SIT as directed by the Commission.
In another case involving the rape and murder of a 10-year-old girl in Maner area of District Patna, the Commission recommended payment of Rs. 5 lakh as relief to the next of kin (NoK) of the victim. In two other cases of death in judicial custody, the Commission observed negligence of jail/ medical officials and recommended relief of Rs.15 lakh.
On Day-2 of the hearing today, the NHRC Chairperson heard 10 cases of alleged bonded labour. The Secretary, Labour, Labour Commissioner and other officers of Bihar Government were present. In one bonded labour case, the Commission expressed its displeasure over a Prison official representing the District Magistrate. In two cases pertaining to child labour, the Commission has directed the Labour Secretary to submit a detailed report as per the format given by the Commission.
In a case of alleged practice of multi-generation bonded labour, the Commission directed the Director General of Investigation, NHRC to conduct an on-the-spot enquiry.
On the same day, the Division Bench of the Commission comprising the Members, Justice (Dr.) Bidyut Ranjan Sarangi and Smt. Vijaya Bharathi Sayani heard 33 cases, which included compliance matters and other complaints of alleged violation of human rights. Three cases not included in the list were taken up out of turn on a mention made by the complainant. During the proceedings, the Commission closed 10 cases after hearing the parties and reviewing compliance reports along with proof of payment of compensation of Rs. 40 lakh to the NoK of the deceased. In five other cases of death in judicial/ police custody wherein the Commission observed negligence of jail/ police officials, monetary relief of Rs. 30 lakh has been recommended. In other matters, further reports have been sought from the authorities.
After the hearing, the Commission interacted with representatives of NGOs, civil society organisations and Human Rights Defenders on important issues pertaining to the State of Bihar. The Chairperson accepted their suggestion for better coordination with the NHRC.
The Commission also held a meeting with senior officers of the State Government. Important issues like non/ delayed submission of reports to the Commission, lack of information among authorities about laws and Supreme Court judgments, issues pertaining to identification, rescue, release and rehabilitation of bonded labourers, violation of human rights by police, crimes against women and children including human trafficking, lack of proper implementation of the prohibition laws and resultant loss of lives, protection of children including child labour, school safety and child welfare, monitoring of shelter homes, correctional institutions and other residential care facilities were discussed. Concluding the Open Hearing and Camp Sitting, the NHRC Chairperson appreciated the officers for their cooperation, which helped in providing relief to the victims.

title: NHRC, India takes suo motu cognizance of the reported sexual harassment of three journalists by Delhi Police personnel during a protest at Jantar Mantar, New Delhi on 3rd October 2026
subtitle: Issues a notice to the Delhi Police Commissioner, calling for a detailed report on the matter within two weeks
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                08 OCT 2026 3:53PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC), India has taken
suo motu
cognizance of a media report that three women journalists were subjected to sexual harassment by Delhi Police personnel during a protest at Jantar Mantar, New Delhi on 3rd October 2026.
The Commission has observed that the contents of the news report, if true, raise serious issues of violation of human rights. Accordingly, it has issued a notice to the Delhi Police Commissioner, calling for a detailed report on the matter within two weeks.
According to the media report, carried on 5
th
October 2026, the New Delhi District Police received complaints about the alleged incidents, which were transferred to the Crime Branch of Delhi Police for an enquiry.

title: NHRC, India takes suo motu cognizance of the reported dilapidated Government Primary School roof supported on benches after the collapse of the main pillar holding it in Darbhanga, Bihar
subtitle: The Commission issues a notice to the Darbhanga District Magistrate, calling for a detailed report on the matter within two weeks
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                08 OCT 2026 3:47PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC), India has taken
suo motu
cognizance of a media report that in Kiratpur of Darbhanga district in Bihar, a Government Primary School roof continues to be temporarily supported by wooden benches, desks and bricks underneath after the main pillar holding it had collapsed three to four months ago. Reportedly, it is a risk to the safety of about 191 students and school staff.
The Commission has observed that the contents of the news report, if true, raise serious issues of human rights violations. Therefore, it has issued a notice to the Darbhanga District Magistrate, calling for a detailed report on the matter within two weeks.
According to the media report carried on 5th October 2026, the administration appears to be unaware of the situation.

title: Government Expands Cancer Medicine Price Controls; Cancer Patients Expected to Save ₹2,500 Crore Annually
ministry: Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers :Department of Pharmaceuticals
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                08 OCT 2026 10:04PM by PIB Delhi
content:
1. Extending price protection to more cancer medicines
Government has approved a cap on the margins charged in the supply and sale of non-scheduled anti-cancer drugs.
These margins will be limited to
30% of the Maximum Retail Price (MRP)
. The measure is expected to reduce medicine prices by
up to 70%
and help cancer patients save
₹2,500 crore annually
, significantly reducing the amount they pay from their own pockets.
Essential cancer medicines included in the scheduled list are already subject to strict government-set ceiling prices. The new decision extends price protection to non-scheduled cancer medicines, which are outside that list, by limiting the margins added before they reach patients.
An expert committee under the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) will finalise the list of medicines to be covered. The National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA) will then take a decision and issue the notification.
2. Reducing the heavy cost of cancer treatment
Cancer incidence is rising in India, with approximately
60 people per one lakh population affected by cancer
. Treatment places a heavy financial burden on patients and their families, who often have to pay substantial amounts from their own pockets.
NPPA’s analysis of market data found that non-scheduled anti-cancer medicines carry an
average price mark-up of approximately 170%
, reaching
700% or more in some cases
. In simple terms, the price rises sharply as the medicine moves through the supply chain before reaching the patient.
Prices also vary significantly depending on whether the medicine is bought from a retail pharmacy, a hospital pharmacy or an online pharmacy.
State authorities, including those in
Maharashtra, Rajasthan and Karnataka
, along with patients and civil society, have raised serious concerns about excessive medicine prices. These concerns have also been voiced on public platforms, particularly over the large gap between the price at which medicines are purchased for sale and the MRP charged to consumers.
Such high margins, especially on expensive cancer medicines, substantially increase patients’ treatment costs. The new cap will curb excessive profiteering, address unfair pricing practices in the market and help ensure fairer prices for patients.
3. Building on the relief delivered by the 2019 decision
The Government’s earlier intervention shows how limiting these margins can bring substantial relief to patients.
In
February 2019
, on the Government’s direction, NPPA capped trade margins on
42 selected non-scheduled anti-cancer drugs
under
Paragraph 19 of the Drugs (Prices Control) Order, 2013
.
That decision reduced MRPs by
up to 91%
, with reported annual savings of
₹984 crore across 526 brands
. It significantly reduced the financial burden on cancer patients and improved their ease of living.
Building on that experience, and addressing the pricing problems identified in the supply chain, the Government has now approved the wider cap. The expected annual savings of ₹2,500 crore will bring further relief to patients undergoing cancer treatment.
4. Maintaining production and ensuring continued availability
To ensure that these life-saving medicines remain available, manufacturers of non-scheduled anti-cancer drugs will be required to
maintain their current production levels
.
The intervention will cover non-scheduled anti-cancer medicines across categories:
branded and generic, domestically produced and imported, and patented and non-patented
. This will help patients significantly benefit from lower prices while ensuring continued availability of the medicines they need.
